[and so forth].

*Ñaṃ īṃ* to the *tasthani* [middle finger], *namaḥ*. *Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ* to the *madhyamā* [middle finger]. *Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ* to the *anāmikā* [ring finger]. *Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ oṃ* to the *kaniṣṭhikā* [pinky]. *Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ āḥ* to both the palms and the backs of the hands. Such is the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*).
[She is] possessed of the radiance of a jasmine flower, adorned with immeasurable ornaments, three-eyed, and holding the *vidyā*, a rosary, a young deer, and a lotus.
One should meditate on the Blessed One’s consort, Matikā, who has the luster of gold and stands at his side, holding a book and a rosary in her lotus-like hands.
She has fifty beautiful limbs, including face, arms, feet, belly, and wings;
her body is radiant, she wears a crown of matted hair adorned with a crescent moon, and she is as white as the moon or jasmine.
With her excellent hands she holds a rosary, a water-pot, and a painting board, and she possesses three eyes.
I bow to her who shines with a form like a lotus, whose youth is unblemished, and who bears the weight of her breasts and hips without effort.

AṂ, homage to the head. ĀṂ, homage to the face. IṂ, homage to the right eye. ĪṂ, homage to the left eye. UṂ, homage to the right ear. ŪṂ, homage to the left ear. ṚṂ, homage to the right nostril. ṜṂ, homage to the left nostril. ḶṂ, homage to the right cheek. ḸṂ, homage to the left cheek. EṂ, homage to the upper lip. AIṂ...

*Namaḥ* to the lower lip. *Oṃ namaḥ* to the upper row of teeth. *Auṃ namaḥ* to the lower row of teeth. *Aṃ namaḥ* to the head. *Aḥ namaḥ* to the throat. *Kaṃ namaḥ* to the right arm. *Khaṃ namaḥ* to the right elbow. *Gaṃ namaḥ* to the right wrist. *Ghaṃ namaḥ* to the right hand. *Ṅaṃ namaḥ* to the fingers of the right hand. *Caṃ namaḥ* to the left arm. *Chaṃ namaḥ* to the left elbow. *Jaṃ namaḥ* to the left wrist. *Jhaṃ namaḥ* to the left hand. *Ñaṃ namaḥ* to the fingers of the left hand. (…) *Ṭaṃ namaḥ* to... [the left foot].
Ṭhaṃ namaḥ at the root of the right thigh; Ḍaṃ namaḥ at the right knee; Ḍhaṃ namaḥ at the tip of the right calf; Ṇaṃ namaḥ at the right foot; Taṃ namaḥ at the toes of the right foot.

Thaṃ namaḥ at the root of the left thigh; Daṃ namaḥ at the left knee; Dhaṃ namaḥ at the tip of the left calf; Naṃ namaḥ at the left foot; Paṃ namaḥ at the toes of the left foot. Phaṃ namaḥ at the right side; Baṃ namaḥ at the left side; Bhaṃ namaḥ at the back; Maṃ namaḥ at the navel; Yaṃ namaḥ at the stomach. Yaṃ *yagātmane* namaḥ at the heart; Raṃ...

*Asṛgātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of blood) at the base of the right arm; *laṃ māṃsātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of flesh) at the base of the left arm; *vaṃ devātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of the divine) on the western petal; *śaṃ asthyātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of bone) at the right armpit; *ṣaṃ majjātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of marrow) at the left armpit; *saṃ śuklātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of semen) at the right foot; *haṃ prāṇātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of vital breath) at the left foot; *laṃ namaḥ* (salutation) from the feet up to the abdomen; *kṣaṃ namaḥ* (salutation) from the mouth up to the abdomen. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*), [one recites]: *Vidmahe mātṛkāṃ caiva, dhīmahi sarasvatyai.* (We know Mātṛkā indeed; we meditate upon Sarasvatī.)

"May that Vāṇī inspire us. One should recite this ten times. One should perform the *vyāpaka-nyāsa* (all-pervading placement) by sequentially placing the syllables upon the following locations: the two ears, the two eyes, the two nostrils, the two cheeks, the two lips, the two roots of the teeth, the head, the face, the two shoulders, the tips of the fingers, the two sides, the back, the navel, the belly, the heart, the roots of the two arms, the other [parts of] the throat and armpits, the heart and so forth, the pair of hands and feet, and the belly and face. Having thus performed the initial placement (*ādi-nyāsa*), the mastery of the recitation of the Gāyatrī will subsequently be attained. Having approached Bhāradvāja, one should pay homage four times.

The deities of the *sandhyā* and so forth: Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, and Sarasvatī are present at the morning *sandhyā*. These four deities, beginning with the *sandhyā*, are declared in their respective order. Their mantra is stated here as [their] individual names in the dative case (*caturthyanta*), preceded by *praṇava* (*oṃ*) and ending with *namaḥ*. One should bow down to them with their respective mantras. Having uttered "To all the deities" (*sarvābhyo devatābhyaḥ*) enclosed by the *praṇava* (*oṃ... oṃ*), and saying "Salutation, salutation" (*namo namaḥ*), one should bow down to all the deities. [Section heading: Offering of Fuel (*samidhādhāna*)]

"Have you committed lust? Have you committed anger? Having said "Salutations! Salutations! and having likewise circumambulated the Goddess, the Brahmin should offer his salutation. Having touched the pair of ears with both hands, and having gently rubbed [the body] from the two knees down to the big toes of the feet, he should salute Gāyatrī and then pay homage to the Lord. The eight directions are declared to be: the east, the south, the west, the north, the zenith, the nadir, the intermediate space, and the earth. One should bow to each of these in a clockwise direction.

Having performed the *sandhyā* with the mantras dedicated to Yama, Viṣṇu, Virūpākṣa, and Savitṛ, facing the southern direction and other respective quarters, the twice-born should then worship his ancestors, elder brothers, and teachers. Thereafter, he should enter the house. Taking the water-vessel (*prokṣaṇī*) filled with water, having arrived at the house, washed his feet, and sipped water (*ācamana*), he should sprinkle the house. Then follows the placing of fuel-sticks (*samidhādhāna*) by the student (*brahmacārin*). Having smeared a square area in a clean place with cow-dung, he should sit there facing the east and sip water.

For the sake of my own well-being and joy, I shall perform the placing of the sacrificial fuel in the morning. Having kindled the fire with the mantra, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan," I strew [grass] around it on the east. With "bhūḥ bhuvaḥ suvaḥ," I strew it around on the south. With "udvayam tamasaḥ pari paśyanta jyotiruttaram | devaṃ devatrā sūryam aganma jyotiruttamam" (Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness, we have gone to Sūrya, the god among gods, the supreme light), I strew it around on the west. [With] "O Agni, come for the feast, being praised... [he strews it around on the north].

"Sit down as the Hotṛ-priest upon the sacrificial grass for the offering of the oblation"—with these words, I strew the grass on the northern side. "Thou art lightning; drive away my sin. O Agni, enjoy this fuel! Today is pure; it is great and unconquered. Producing smoke, he touches the divine summit with his rays that are like the peaks of mountains. Following that, [he reaches] the sun. O Aditi, give thy consent; O Anumati, give thy consent; O Sarasvatī, give thy consent; O God Savitṛ, impel the oblation of fuel! (l3. *Bhūḥ* svāhā! This is for Agni. *Bhuvaḥ* svāhā! This is for Vāyu.

This, O Sky, Svāhā! To Sūrya this. Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Suvaḥ Svāhā! To Prajāpati this. You are rain; cut away my evil. Be pleased with us, [O] Sūrya. By Aditi you have been approved. (L4. By Anumati you have been approved. By Sarasvatī you have been approved. O God Savitṛ, you have impelled [us]. "Svāhā!"—having thus placed the fuel-stick, there is the ritual worship (*upasthāna*).

Rising, [he says]: "O Agni, that which is your splendor (*tejas*), by that may I become splendid; that which is your luster (*varcas*) in Agni, by that may I become lustrous; that which is your vigor (*haras*) in Agni, by that may I..."
May I be possessed of vigor; may Agni bestow upon me wisdom, upon me progeny, and upon me splendor; may Indra bestow upon me wisdom, upon me progeny, and upon me sensory power;
may Sūrya bestow upon me wisdom, upon me progeny, and upon me radiance.

O God, with a good path for our wealth, lead us through all ways of knowledge; remove from us the crooked sin; we shall offer to you the most abundant word of homage. Homage to Agni! [Whatever was] deficient in mantra...

"O Consumer of Oblations, whatever has been offered by me that is deficient in ritual action or deficient in devotion—may that, O God, be complete unto You. Indeed, among all the various atonements consisting of asceticism and ritual acts, the supreme one is the constant remembrance of Śrī Śiva. Having prostrated and saluted: "O sir! Taking up the sacred ash (*bhasman*), he consecrates it with the mantra: "May you not harm our children, nor our offspring, nor our life-span; may you not harm our cattle, nor our horses. Do not slay our heroes in your wrath, O Rudra! Bearing oblations, we serve you with delight. Thus, having consecrated [the ash].

"May I be intelligent," on the forehead; "may I be radiant," on the heart; "may I be glorious," on the right shoulder; "may I be possessed of Vedic splendor," on the left shoulder; "may I be long-lived," on the head; "may there be well-being," on the eyes. [The recitation of these mantras follows. Immediately thereafter, one performs the pure sipping of water (*ācamana*).
[Now begins the *aupāsana* rite for the householder.]

Having washed his feet, sipped water, sat down in a clean place, and performed breath-control (*prāṇāyāma*), he should maintain [the fire]; in the case where it is to be maintained, having established the sacred fire (*agni*), he makes the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*). In the case where the fire is to be deposited in the fuel-sticks (*samitsamāropaṇa*), having established the common fire (*laukikāgni*), there is the dismissal of the fire from the fuel-sticks (*samidagnivisarjana*). Having placed a fuel-stick [into the fire] with the mantra: "Being invoked, fair-faced Agni, sit upon your own womb in the east; sit here in this higher assembly-place, O All-Gods (*viśvedevāḥ*) and the sacrificer. Thus, having placed the fuel-stick.

"O awakened Agni, wake up this man; unite him with his sacrifices and pious works, and restore him to his former state. Making you a young father again, may I follow after you as a son; may that thread of mine be woven in you. Having thus prayed, the *saṅkalpa* (resolution) follows: "For the sake of destroying my accumulated sins (*durita*) and for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (*parameśvara*), I shall perform the morning *aupāsana-homa*. Touching water: For the venerable Agni, the Great Mantra: the venerable Agastya is the *ṛṣi*; *anuṣṭubh* is the meter; Hutāśana (the Fire-god) is the deity; *Raṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*); *svāhā* is the power (*śakti*); *Maṃ*...

The Kīlaka: The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of attaining all my desired goals during the *aupāsana* rite. *Oṃ svasti pūrṇamukhātmane aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ* (Salutation to the Self whose face is full and auspicious, with both thumbs). *Oṃ darśapūrṇātmane tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ* (Salutation to the Self of the New and Full Moon sacrifices, with both index fingers). *Oṃ cāturmāsyātmane madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ* (Salutation to the Self of the Four-Monthly sacrifices, with both middle fingers). *Oṃ dhūmrākṣāya anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ* (Salutation to Dhūmrākṣa, with both ring fingers). *Oṃ sahasraśīrṣe kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ namaḥ* (Salutation to the Thousand-Headed One, with both little fingers). *Oṃ saptajihvātmane karatalakarapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ* (Salutation to the Self of the Seven Tongues, with palms and backs of hands). Thus is the ritual placement on the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*).
I shall now explain the meditation on fire for the sake of accomplishing all purposes of the *homa* sacrifice:
it has two faces, one heart, four ears, and two nostrils.
He has two faces, six eyes, is tawny in color, and possesses seven hands;
he is endowed with three girdles, three feet, and seven tongues.
He has four horns, is mounted upon a bull, and possesses a radiance equal to the rising sun;
he has four hands on his right side and three hands on his left.
In his right hands, he holds a sacrificial ladle (*sruk*), a sacrificial spoon (*sruva*), a rosary (*akṣamālā*), and a spear (*śakti*).
A spear and a fan, and a vessel of ghee, in the left [hands].
One should meditate upon the god Agni, who bears [the oblation] directed toward oneself.
He has four horns, three feet, two heads, and seven hands;
he is bound in three ways, the bull bellows, the great god has entered into mortals.
For this god pervades all the quarters; he was indeed born first within the excellent womb.
The one who has been born, the one who is being born, and the one yet to be born stands facing westward, with faces turned in every direction.

(*14*) In the fire-worship, [one offers] in the directions starting from the east into the fire: *Homage to Agni*; *homage to Jātavedas*; *homage to Sahojas*; *homage to Ajirāprabhava*; *homage to Vaiśvānara*; *homage to Nayyāpas*; *homage to Pañcaktirāyas*. (*15*) *Homage to Visarpiṇ*. In the center, *homage to Yajñapuruṣa*. Having thus worshipped, [one recites]: *juṣasvanaḥ*. (+)

Having performed the strewing around of the sun, having recited from "devasya tvā" up to "barhiṣi," and having strewn [the grass] all around, [he says]: "Aditi, give your consent; Anumati, give your consent; Sarasvatī, give your consent; O God Savitṛ, impel [us]. Salutation to Indra; salutation to Yama; salutation to Varuṇa; salutation to Soma; salutation to Agni; salutation to Nirṛti; salutation to Vāyu; salutation to Īśāna; salutation to Agni; salutation to the Self; salutation to all the Brāhmaṇas.

Having thus worshipped with the mantra, "Thou art lightning; dispel [my] evil," and having placed a fuel-stick (*samidh*) into the fire while requesting the members of the assembly, saying, "I shall offer," and having received their permission with the words, "Offer!"; he offers in the center: "To Sūrya, svāhā! To Sūrya, this [belongs], not mine. The northern oblation is slightly larger: "To Prajāpati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, this [belongs], not mine," offered slightly toward the northeast. If the two oblations have become mixed, he says, "I shall offer the *vanaspati* oblation for the sake of the expiation of eight thousand oblations," and where you know...

"O Lord of the Forest, the secret names of the gods are there; desire the oblations [to be offered] therein. Having placed a fuel-stick (*samidh*) as before, he should perform two oblations (*āhuti*) without a mantra. "You are rain; cut off my fever; take pleasure in the voice of the Sun. You have gone forth with Aditi; you have gone forth with Anumati; you have gone forth with Sarasvatī. O God Savitṛ, you have impelled [us]. Having placed a fuel-stick, [he performs] the standing worship (*upasthāna*). "What we may offer to you, O Agni... "Homage to Agni. [This is] the recollection of the mantra...

Having paid homage, I salute [thee]. This is the mantra for the case of rekindling the fire: "O Agni, thou who art led by the priests, having been born, thou didst shine; knowing that, O Agni, ascend [the fire] and increase the kindler... Having taken hold of the fire with the tip [of the fuel], [he recites]:

"For the sake of union, the great Sāman, the sovereign power, the faith, the virility, the Triṣṭubh, the vigor, the adorned one, the fierce hero—Indra with the fifteen-fold Stoma, this middle [space], together with Vāta and Sagara, protect [us]."

Having thus placed [the fire] on the forehead, one should perform the pure sipping of water (*śuddhācamana*). In the case of the rite of self-installation (*ātmasamāropaṇa*), [one recites] the mantra for the dismissal of the fire from oneself: "Descend again, O Jātavedas, to the gods; may he, knowing well, grant us great prosperity. Grant us long life, progeny, and wealth; come with good guidance, O Agni, never departing, [granting] strength. Having thus dismissed the fire abiding in oneself into the common worldly fire (*laukikāgni*), one should proceed as before. This is the mantra for self-installation: "O Agni, that body of yours which is worthy of sacrifice..."

"O Agni, ascending, bring wealth to this [sacrificer]; O Jātavedas, having become the sacrifice, come to the sacrifice, to your own womb, being born; come to your abode. Having thus taken the blazing fire into himself, he should perform the remainder as before. When performing the evening *aupāsana* rite, one should make the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) on the previous day:

"Together with the evening *aupāsana* of yesterday, I shall offer the morning *aupāsana-homa* of today. [Then follows] the expiation for the non-performance prior to the principal oblation: "O Agni... (p19a).

F16b. Side-heading: *Bhuktaprāyaścitta* (Expiation for Eating). [L1] *Nakabhi* … *bṛhatyamitvamayā asi | agrasā manasā dhṛto'yasā havyam ūhiṣe yānothehi bheṣajaṃ svāhā | agnaye ayasa idaṃ na mama*. Having thus offered an oblation of clarified butter (*ājya*), or in its absence, a fuel-stick (*samidh*), and having placed a fuel-stick [on the fire], one should perform two evening oblations; then two morning oblations must be performed. If one has eaten at night through ignorance, [the expiation is performed] in the morning.

Having performed the expiation for non-performance (*akaraṇaprāyaścitta*), one should make the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "I shall perform the expiation for having eaten. [Then follows] an oblation of clarified butter (*ājyāhuti*); in its absence, fuel-sticks (*samidhaḥ*). "O Gods, whatever vows of yours we, being more ignorant than the wise, have violated, may Agni, the knowing one, make that right through those seasons by which he ordains the gods. If it is morning, then having bathed and made the resolve: "I shall perform the expiation for having eaten," [one recites]: "O Puruṣatrāyiṣṭha, whatever we, being ignorant, have done against you, forgive us for that."

"O Agni, you have loosened on all sides the bonds of Aditi, the sinless one"—having thus reflected upon what must be done, the procedure for the *aupāsana* rite in the absence [of the wife] is as follows: having lifted the worldly fire with the syllable *praṇava*, having brought it back with the verse "After Agni," and having deposited it with the verse "In the highest heaven," one should perform the oblation with four wood-shavings (*śakala*). One should offer [the oblation] with the verse "Of Savitṛ...
[and] "That wondrous favor of the most excellent Savitṛ, which benefits all people, which Kaṇva milked forth—the swelling, thousand-streamed flow of milks, O great ones. All... (l6).

"O God Savitṛ, impel us today... (*nideva savitaḥ suva*). "O God Savitṛ, impel us today... (*adhyā no deva savitaḥ*)—this is to be recited with the same distinctions as before. There are the acts of ascending and descending, as well as the scraping (*ullekhana*). One should perform this daily.
After the *homa* offering, it is the time for fetching the fuel-sticks (*samidh*), flowers, and *darbha* grass. (P19b, f17a, sideheading: Fetching the Fuel-sticks etc., Midday Ritual; l1).

Having recited "May [I obtain] life, strength, fame, and splendor according to my desire" (*yatheṣṭam āyur balam yaśo varcaḥ... vanaspate*), and having performed the remembrance of the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevasmaraṇa*) while departing from the place of origin, [one should perform] the placing of flowers and the placing of *darbha* grass.

"Salutations to the Darbha-grass and the Svastika, which dispel all sins and are embraced by the Supreme Lord born from the nose of Viriñca. Then, one should perform the study of the Vedas and other such duties.

After that, the materials for the meal should be prepared. Having prepared them, when eleven *nāḍīs* have passed [since sunrise], one should perform the midday rites (*mādhyāhnika*). Taking the necessary materials such as clay and so forth, one should go to a river or similar place as before; with sacred grass (*pavitra*) in hand, having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*), and having bathed as before, one should discard the wet garment, put on a white garment, and also an upper cloth (*uttarīya*).

Having held [the water], washed his feet, and sipped water (*ācamana*), he should wring out his wet garment at the conclusion of the *brahmayajña*. Having performed the application of sacred ash (*vibhūti*) as before and made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*), he should first perform the ninefold sprinkling with the hymn beginning "āpo hi ṣṭhā. Then, reciting: "May the waters purify the earth; purified by the earth, may they purify me. May Brahmaṇaspati purify me; purified by the Veda, may he purify me.

Whatever is left-over, whatever is unfit to be eaten, or whatever evil deed I have committed—may the waters purify all that in me, and [purify] the acceptance of gifts from the virtuous, svāhā! Having sipped water as before, [he concludes].

Having purified oneself with the *dadhikrāviṇṇo* verses and sprinkled water clockwise, with an upright body, one should offer a single *arghya* as before, perform the *prāyaścitta-arghya*, and the withdrawal of the weapon (*astrasaṃhāra*). Having circumambulated clockwise as before, one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*) for Āditya and others, sip water (*ācamana*), and perform a salutation (*vandana*). Then, having come to the place of recitation (*japasthāna*), having paid homage and seated facing east, one should perform *prāṇāyāma* as before, invoke Gāyatrī, and recite her [mantra] one hundred and eight times while keeping the hands level with the chest. Finally, having performed *prāṇāyāma* again—

Having dismissed the Gāyatrī, one should rise. For the mantra beginning with *ā satyena*, the seers are Ka-vyā and others; the meters are Triṣṭubh and others; the deity is Bhāskara; the application is for the worship of Sūrya.

Looking at the sun with arms raised and the *vyoma-mudrā*, one should recite: *Ā satyena rajasā vartamāno niveśayann amṛtaṃ martyaṃ ca hiraṇyayena savitā rathenā devo yāti bhuvanāni paśyan.* *Ud vayaṃ tamasas pari paśyanto jyotir uttaram | devaṃ devatrā sūryam aganma jyotir uttamam.* *Ut* [is for] Jñātavedas.

The banners bear the god Sūrya so that everyone may behold him. Wondrous has the god risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. He has filled the earth and the broad mid-air; Sūrya is the soul of all that moves and stands. That eye, established by the gods, has risen bright in the east. May we see for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns; may we rejoice for a hundred autumns; may we delight for a hundred autumns; may we be for a hundred autumns; may we hear well for a hundred autumns; may we proclaim for a hundred autumns.

May we be unconquered for a hundred autumns; may we behold the light of the sun. May that Sūrya—who has risen from the great ocean, shining forth from the midst of the flowing [waters], whose eyes are like the sun, and who gazes upon all—purify me with his salutation. Oṃ... (meditation... as before.
Having paid homage to all, one should sit down.
[Now, the primary time for the Brahmayajña.]

Having washed his feet and hands and performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*), holding *darbha* grass in his hand, he makes this formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*): "I shall perform the sacrifice of the Vedic study (*brahmayajña*). Then, touching the water, he places the two hands, with the *darbha* blades still held, upon his right thigh, keeping the right hand uppermost. He recites: *oṃ bhūḥ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ | oṃ bhuvaḥ bhargodevasya dhīmahi | oṃ suvaḥ dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt |* *oṃ bhūḥ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ mahi | oṃ bhuvaḥ dhiyo...*

May the divine Savitṛ impel [our intellect]. Oṃ *suvaḥ*; may that Savitṛ impel [us]. Oṃ, I praise Agni, the domestic priest (*purohita*), the god who is the officiating priest (*ṛtvij*) of the sacrifice, the invoker (*hotṛ*), the bestower of treasures. Having performed the recitation (*japa*) beginning with "O Vāyu, come hither; O Medha, come hither; may Savitṛ impel you toward the most excellent rite," and ending with the first question, one should recite the second question on the following day in this same sequence: Oṃ, being summoned as the leader, O carrier of oblations, sit down as the invoker upon the sacred grass (*barhis*). Oṃ, may the divine waters be auspicious for our protection.

"May they come to us for the drinking of Soma and for renown. Reciting three times: "Oṃ, obeisance to Brahman; obeisance be to Agni; obeisance to the Earth; obeisance to the plants; obeisance to Speech; obeisance to the Lord of Speech;

obeisance to the Great Viṣṇu, I perform [this]. Then, touching water while reciting: "Oṃ, that is Truth; I offer this into the fire of austerity and faith. You are rain; destroy my evil. From untruth I have gone to truth. [The Summary]

I shall perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*) as an ancillary part of the *brahmayajña*. [Wearing the sacred thread] over the right shoulder (*nivīti*): I satiate Prajāpati, the seer of the section (*kāṇḍarṣi*). I satiate Soma, the seer of the section. I satiate Soma, the seer of the section. I satiate Agni, the seer of the section. I satiate the Viśvedevas, the seers of the section. I satiate Svayambhū, the seer of the section. I satiate Sadasaspati. I satiate Sāvitrī. I satiate Gāyatrī. I satiate the Metres (*chandāṃsi*). I satiate the Ṛgveda. I satiate the Yajurveda. I satiate the Sāmaveda.

I satiate the Sāmaveda; I satiate the Atharvaveda; I satiate the Atharvāṅgiras; I satiate the Itihāsas and Purāṇas; I satiate all the classes of gods; I satiate all beings. 17. Then, having adjusted the sacred thread over the left shoulder and sipped water, I shall perform the daily libation (*nityatarpaṇa*). I satiate Agni, Prajāpati, Sthāṇu, Rudra, Aditi, Bṛhaspati, and the Serpents—these deities of the eastern door, together with the constellations, the days and nights, and the muhūrtas. I satiate the Vasus; [and] the Pitṛs...

I gratify Aryaman, Bhaga, Savitṛ, Tvaṣṭṛ, Vāyu, Indra, and Agni—these deities of the southern gate, together with the constellations, the houses, the days and nights, and the muhūrtas. I also gratify the Rudras. I gratify Mitra, Indra, the Great Ancestors (Mahāpitṛs), the Waters (Āpas), the Viśvedevas, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu—these deities of the western gate. I also gratify the Ādityas. [I gratify] the Vasus, Varuṇa, Aja Ekapād, Ahirbudhnya, Pūṣan, the Aśvins, and Yama—these deities of the northern gate.

I satisfy the deities together with the constellations, the planets, the days and nights, and the muhūrtas. I satisfy the Sādhyas. I satisfy Brahmā, Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, Hiraṇyagarbha, the four-faced one, and the Self-existent One. [I satisfy] the attendants of Brahmā, the female attendants of Brahmā, Agni, Vāyu, Varuṇa, Soma, Sūrya, and Candramas. I satisfy the constellations. Oṃ Bhūḥ Puruṣa! Oṃ Bhuvaḥ Puruṣa! Oṃ Suvaḥ Puruṣa!

Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ Puruṣa! Oṃ bhūḥ! Oṃ bhuvaḥ! Oṃ suvaḥ! Oṃ mahaḥ! Oṃ janaḥ! Oṃ tapaḥ! Oṃ satyam! [I bow to] the god Bhava; the god Śarva; the god Īśāna; the god Paśupati; the god Rudra; the god Ugra; the god Bhīma; the god Mahānta. [I bow to] the wife of the god Bhava; the wife of the god Śarva; the wife of the god Īśāna; the wife of the god Paśupati; the son of the god Rudra; the wife of the god Ugra.

The wife of the god Bhīma; the wife of the great god; the son of the god Bhava; the son of the god Śarva; the son of the god Īśāna; the son of the god Paśupati; the son of the god Rudra; the son of the fierce (ugra) ... god Bhīma; the son of the great god; the Rudras; the attendants of Rudra; the female attendant of Rudra; Sanatkumāra; Skanda; Indra; Jayanta; Ṣaṣṭhī; the six-faced one; Viśākha; Mahāsena.

To Subrahmaṇya; to the attendants of Skanda; to Skanda … the obstacle-maker; to Vināyaka; to Vīra; to Śūra; to Varada; to Hastimukha; to Lambodara; to Ekadanta; to the attendants of Vighna; to the female attendants of Vighna; to Keśava; to Nārāyaṇa; to Mādhava; to Govinda; to Viṣṇu; to Madhusūdana; to Trivikrama; to Vāmana; to Śrīdhara; to Hṛṣīkeśa; to Padmanābha; to Dāmodara; to Saṅkarṣaṇa; to Vāsudeva; to Pra … [the rest of the names].
Viṣṇu; the goddess Śrī; the goddess Hrī; the goddess Puṣṭi; the goddess Kṛtiṣṭi; the goddess Sarasvatī; the attendants of Viṣṇu; the female attendants of Viṣṇu;
Kāla; Nīla; Mṛtyu; Antaka; [the King] Citra; Citragupta; Vaivasvata; the attendants of Vaivasvata; the female attendants of Vaivasvata;
Bhāradvāja; Gautama; Atri; Āṅgīrasa; Durgā; Jyeṣṭhā; Dhanvantari; the attendants of Dhanvantari.

(l4. The attendants of Dhanvantari. Then, with the sacred thread suspended around the neck (nivīti): the seer (ṛṣi), the great seer (paramarṣi), the divine seer (devarṣi), the brahmin seer (brahmarṣi), the royal seer (rājarṣi), the vaiśya seer (vaiśyarṣi), the śūdra seer (śūdarṣi), the human seer (janarṣi), the ascetic seer (taparṣi), the seven seers (saptarṣi), the section-seer (kāṇḍarṣi), (l5. the wife of a seer (ṛṣipatnī), the daughter of a seer (ṛṣiputrā), the granddaughter of a seer (ṛṣipautrā), ...
Bodhāyana, Āpastamba, the author of the Sūtras, Satyāṣāḍha, Hiraṇyakeśin, the Vājasaneyin, Yājñavalkya, Āśvalāyana.
I satiate Śaunaka; Vyāsa; (p22b, f20a, l1) the *praṇava*; the *vyāhṛtis*; the *sāvitrī*; the *gāyatrī*; the meters; the *Ṛgveda*; the *Yajurveda*; the *Sāmaveda*;

the *Atharvaveda*; the *Atharvāṅgirases*; the *Itihāsas* and *Purāṇas*; all the divine beings; and all living creatures. (l2) I satiate the ancestors with *svadhā* and obeisance; I satiate the grandfathers with *svadhā* and obeisance; I satiate the great-grandfathers with *svadhā* and obeisance; [and] the mothers with *svadhā*.

Salutations; I satiate: the paternal grandfather, the paternal great-grandfather, the maternal grandfathers, the maternal great-grandfathers, the maternal grandmother, the maternal paternal grandmother, the maternal great-grandmother, the teachers, the wives of the teachers, the *kurus*, the wives of the gurus, the friends, the wives of the friends, the kinsmen, the ministers, [the wives of] the ministers—all of them, all of them. *Svadhā*; salutations; I satiate. But one whose father is living shall satiate: Kavyavāhana, Anala, Soma, Yama, Aryaman, and the Agniṣvāttas.

To the Soma-drinkers... having sipped water (*ācamya*), [he says]: "Wherever the resting place may be for those whose selves are afflicted by hunger and thirst, may this water with sesame seeds (*tilodaka*) offered to them be inexhaustible.

"Carrying strength, nectar, ghee, milk, ambrosia, and flowing essence—*svadhā* be to you... [reciting this], he offers a handful of water (*jalāñjali*) on the bank, saying: "Be satisfied! Be satisfied! Having sat down and sipped water, he takes his wet garment, folds it fourfold, and [proceeds].

He says: "Whoever among us... and so forth. Having squeezed [the water], having sprinkled the place of recitation (*japasthāna*), he should enter the house. Having washed his feet... some praise the worship of Viṣṇu; others, the worship of Śiva; others, the worship of both; others, the worship of the five images (*pañcaberayajana*); and some, the worship of one's chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*). Such is the option. We, however, perform the worship of Śiva with his retinue (*saparivāraśivayajana*). Having prepared a place of worship in a clean spot smeared with cow dung, and having uttered the root mantra (*mūlamantra*)...
Having sat upon a seat facing north in the presence of Śiva, and having meditated upon Gaurī, the Guru, and Sadāśiva, one should perform the concentration on the breath (*prāṇadhāraṇa*).
[Now follows the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*):]

Today, by the command of the Blessed Lord Mahādeva, for the sake of destroying all my sins produced by ignorance and karma, and for the sake of purifying the body, I shall perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). (…) (l5. (…) The Blessed Nārāyaṇa is the seer (*ṛṣi*); *prakṛti-puruṣa* is the meter (*chandas*); Satya is the deity (*devatā*). Having recited "oṃ laṃ" eight times and performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), one should recite: "O Earth, be pleasant, a protector, a dwelling place, vast and wide. Having uttered this, [one visualizes] the square earth-maṇḍala from the feet up to the knees.

[The element] of dark-green color: I dissolve it into water. Having recited "Oṃ Vaṃ" eight times, [one says]: "O Vāta, that treasure of nectar which is placed in your house, from that grant us life; from that bestow upon us medicine. From that bring us great prosperity. May Vāta blow forth medicines, auspicious for our bodies and beneficial for our hearts. May he not harm our lifespan. Having uttered this, one dissolves the sphere of water—from the knees up to the navel, shaped like a half-moon and white in color—into fire. [Recite] "Oṃ Raṃ" eight times.

Having recited: "O Agni, you ward off the *rakṣas* with your bright luster, O immortal one; pure, purifying, and wise," one should dissolve the triangular, red-colored circle of light from the navel up to the heart into the wind element. Having recited "Oṃ... eight times, and having recited:
"O you who carry the medicine of the wind, you who carry away disease; for you, the universal healer, act as the messenger of the gods," [one should dissolve it] from the heart up to the throat.

I dissolve the smoke-colored, six-cornered wind-maṇḍala into space. Having recited "oṃ haṃ" eight times, and having uttered: "Truth, knowledge, infinite is Brahman; he who knows that which is hidden in the secret cave, in the supreme heaven—he together with the wise Brahman attains all desires," one should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma) and join the space-maṇḍala, circular in shape and dark blue in color, from the throat up to the head at the "twelve-finger limit" (dvādaśānta) within the Supreme Brahman.

Having joined [the breath] in this manner, one should visualize the heart-lotus as facing downward. Then, having severed the five knots located at the knees, the navel, the heart, the throat, the space between the eyebrows, and the *brahmarandhra* with the *praṇava* (Oṃ) and the *vajramudrā*, and having turned the heart-lotus upward by means of the *praṇava-prāṇāyāma*, one should visualize it blossoming by reciting the *praṇava* and the *vyāhṛtis*. Then, having uttered: "He who stands below the navel at a distance of one span, above that is Brahman; he is Śiva, he is Hari, he is Indra, he is the Supreme Sound (*paramasvara*)."

Having joined the individual soul (jīvātman) residing in the heart-lotus with the Supreme Brahman at the "twelve-finger limit" (dvādaśānta) by means of the *praṇava* through the path of the *suṣumnā* while employing the *yonimudrā*, one should meditate upon the Person of Sin (*pāpapuruṣa*). One should contemplate that black figure in the belly as having the murder of a Brāhmaṇa for its head, the theft of gold for its two arms, the drinking of liquor associated with its heart, and violating the Guru’s bed for its two hips. Its feet are bound by association with those [sins], and its limbs and minor members are the various mortal sins (*pātaka*). Its body hair consists of minor offenses (*upapātaka*), and its beard and eyes are smeared with them. He holds a sword and a shield; thus one should contemplate the sin. Having reflected in this manner:

Having made the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*): "I shall perform the drying, burning, flooding, condensing, and disintegration of this person composed of sins committed through mind, speech, and body by means of their respective mantras," one should recite the syllable *Yam*, the seed-syllable of wind. Its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Kiṣku, its meter (*chandas*) is Jagatī, and its deity (*devatā*) is Vāyu. Its application (*viniyoga*) is in the drying of the body of the person of sin. Having recited *Yam* eight times, one should fill [the breath] through the left nostril; having recited it sixteen times, one should perform *kumbhaka* (retention of breath) with the wind residing at the navel.

Having visualized the body of the *pāpapuruṣa* (the personification of sin) as withered, one should then recite [the seed-syllable] eight times and exhale through the right nostril. For the fire-seed syllable *Raṃ*: Kāśyapa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), *triṣṭubh* is the meter (*chandas*), Rudra is the deity (*devatā*), and Jātavedas Agni is the deity; its application (*viniyoga*) is for the burning of the body of the *pāpapuruṣa*. Having repeated *Śaṃ* eight times, one should inhale through the right nostril, recite it sixteen times, perform breath-retention (*kumbhaka*), and visualize the body of the *pāpapuruṣa* being consumed by the digestive fire (*jāṭharāgni*). Then, having recited it eight times—

One should expel [the breath] through the left nostril. Regarding the seed-syllable *vaṃ*: Vasiṣṭha and Hiraṇyagarbha are the seers (*ṛṣi*); Triṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*); the Supreme Self, Varuṇa, and Viṣṇu are the deities (*devatā*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the bathing with nectar the burnt body of the personified sin. Having repeated "vaṃ" eight times, one should fill [the lungs] through the left nostril;

having recited it sixteen times and performed the retention (*kumbhaka*), one should recite "vaṃ" three times. Thus, the burnt body is bathed by the stream of nectar flowing from the lunar light of consciousness (*ciccandrikā*) at the crown of the head.

Having meditated [on this], one should recite "laṃ" eight times and exhale through the right nostril. For the seed-syllable of Earth, "laṃ," Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the *gāyatrī* is the meter (*chanda*), and Nārāyaṇa in the form of the Boar is the deity (*devatā*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the consolidation of our body. Having recited "laṃ" eight times, one should fill [the breath] through the right nostril; having recited it sixteen times, one should perform the retention (*kumbhaka*). Then, having meditated on the body as consolidated, one should recite [the syllable] eight times.

One should expel [the air] through the left nostril. For the *māyābīja* "Śrīm," Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the *gāyatrī* is the meter (*chanda*), and Lakṣmī is the deity (*devatā*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is in the ritual of forming the limbs, beginning with the head. Having recited "Śrīm" eight times, one should fill [the breath] through the left nostril, perform sixteen rounds of breath-retention (*kumbhaka*), and then recite: "Śrī and Lakṣmī are your two wives; day and night are your two sides; the stars are your form; the Aśvins are your manifestation; may I attain what is desired; may I attain that [person]; may I attain everything."

Having recited [the mantra], one should visualize the head, hands, feet, and other limbs [of the deity] and exhale through the right nostril. One should visualize one’s own body being drenched with nectar by golden jars filled with ambrosial water, held in the hands of celestial women adorned with every ornament. Having thus visualized the body as bathed in nectar, one should contemplate its divine form. [One should think: "From the presence of the Supreme Brahman, I cause the sphere of space (*ākāśamaṇḍala*) to reach its proper place; from space, the sphere of wind (*vāyumaṇḍala*); from wind, fire (*agni*)."

(-) Having visualized the spheres of the five elements—*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*, *agnerāpaḥ*, *adbhyaḥ pṛthivīmaṇḍalam*—each brought to its respective location; then, having led the individual soul (*jīvātman*) from the Supreme Brahman at the *dvādaśānta* through the path of the *suṣumnā* by means of the *tri-yoni-mudrā* and the *praṇava* into the heart-lotus, one should visualize it as having entered there: "Born from the root-stalk of Dharma, beautifully adorned with the stalk of Knowledge, endowed with the eight petals of Sovereignty, and possessing the pericarp of supreme Dispassion."

In the center of the pericarp of that lotus, one should meditate upon the Lord as the syllable Oṃ, having the form of a pure flame of a lamp, incomparable, and the size of a thumb. Having thus meditated, one should perform the pervasion (*vyāpaka*) three times with the *praṇava* (Oṃ). Of this venerable *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are the seers (*ṛṣayaḥ*). The *Ṛg*, *Yajur*, *Sāma*, and *Atharva* Vedas are the meters (*chandāṃsi*).

The supreme life-force (*prāṇa-śakti*), the creator of the entire universe, is the deity (*devatā*). *Ām* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*); *hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*); *kroṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*). The application (*viniyoga*) is in the recitation for the purpose of my consecration. *Ām*.

To the two thumbs, *namaḥ*. *Hrīṃ* to the two index fingers. *Kroṃ* to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*. (p26a., f23b., l1. *Śrīṃ* to the head, whose essence is sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. *Kroṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), whose essence is the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose. *Kroṃ* to the single [armor] (*kavaca*) for speech, feet, hands, anus, and genitals. *Srīṃ* to the eyes, whose essence is speaking, giving, moving, excreting, and procreating.
(l2. *Āṃ* to the weapon (*astra*), whose essence is mind, intellect, ego, and consciousness; *phaṭ*. *Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ oṃ*, thus is the binding of the directions (*digbandha*).
In meditation,
she is seated upon a red lotus shining with the heat of a lake of crimson water;
her lotus-hands hold a noose, a bow made of sugarcane, a jeweled bowstring, a goad, and the five arrows.

May the Supreme Power of Life (Prāṇa-śakti), who bears a skull-bowl at the corners of her mouth, who is radiant with three eyes, enriched by full breasts, and possesses the hue of the rising sun— may that Goddess bring us happiness.

The root mantra: *Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa hoṃ haṃsassohaṃ*. "May my vital breath (*prāṇa*) remain here; may my life-force (*jīva*) remain here; [may] all my senses—speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, voice, feet, hands, anus, and genitals—along with the intellect (*buddhi*), ego (*ahaṅkāra*), and consciousness (*citta*), having come here, dwell happily for a long time. *Svāhā kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ haṃsassohaṃ*. Having recited this ten times, then...

One should perform the daily ritual placement (*mahanyāsa*) as an ancillary part of the worship of Śiva. [Section heading: *Mahanyāsa*. Now, therefore, we shall explain the procedure for the recitation, fire-oblation, worship, and consecration of the five-limbed Rudras, preceded by ritual placement (*nyāsa*). "O Rudra, that which is yours..."—this is for the crest-lock (*śikhā*); "O Rudra, that which is yours..."—[repeated]. "Homage to Rudra" is for the crest-lock.

"In this great ocean..."—this is for the head (*śiras*). "In this great ocean, in the intermediate space..."—[repeated]. "Of them..."—[repeated]. "We meditate upon that..."—[repeated]. "Homage to Bhava" is for the head.

"Thousands upon thousands" on the forehead: "To those thousands upon thousands on my forehead, to the Rudras, obeisance. "The swan dwelling in purity" between the eyebrows: "The swan dwelling in purity... the great. Between the eyebrows, "to the Haṃsa, obeisance. "We worship Tryambaka" on the three eyes: "We worship Tryambaka... from death to immortality. On the two eyes, "to Tryambaka, obeisance. "Obeisance to Sṛtya" and so forth on the two ears: "Obeisance to Sṛtya and to Vaiśanta. On the two ears, "to Sṛtya-hirūpa Rudra, obeisance."

With the mantra "mā nastoke," [one should touch] the nose. "mā nastoke mate | nāsikāyāṃ rudrāya namaḥ" (O Rudra, do not harm our children or our wives; obeisance to Rudra on the nose). With "avatatya," [one should touch] the mouth. "avatatya dhanustvaṃ (+) bhava | mukhe sahasrākṣāya namaḥ" (Having unstrung your bow, O thousand-eyed one, be gracious;

obeisance to the thousand-eyed one on the mouth). The two blue-necked ones are on the throat. "nīlagrīvāḥ śitikaṇṭhā (+) carāḥ | teṣāṃ (l5. sahasra (+) tanmasi | kaṇṭhe nīlagrīvebhyo namaḥ" (The blue-necked, white-throated ones who roam; of them, we meditate upon a thousand-fold [host]; obeisance to the blue-necked ones on the throat). "The blue-necked, white-throated ones who dwell in heaven (+) tāḥ | teṣāṃ (+) tanmasi | upakaṇṭhe nīlagrīvebhyo namaḥ" (Those who are in heaven; of them, we meditate upon a thousand-fold [host]; obeisance to the blue-necked ones near the throat). "namaste" (obeisance to you).

With the mantra "May there be [salutation] to your weapon," he places it on the two upper arms. With "Salutation to your weapon, to the bow," [he says] "Salutation to the weapons, the arms, and the bows" upon the two upper arms. With "That missile of yours," he places it on the two forearms. With "That missile of yours, O arm," [he says] "Salutation to the missile" upon the two forearms. With "Those which are the sacred fords," he places it on the two hands.

With "Those which are the sacred fords, the devourers," [he says] "To them we pay homage" and "Salutation to Rudra in the hand. Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the five sections beginning with "Sadyojāta" upon the five fingers.

[With] the two thumbs and the two index fingers: *sadyojātaṃ bhavāya namaḥ*; [with] the two thumbs: *sadyojātāya namaḥ*; [with] the two thumbs and the [remaining] fingers beginning with the index finger:

*vāmadevāya nmanāya namaḥ*; [with] the two index fingers: *vāmadevāya namaḥ*; [with] the two middle fingers: *aghorebhyo rūpebhyaḥ*; *aghorāya namaḥ*; [with] the two ring fingers: *tatpuruṣāya vidmahe*; *tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*; [with] the two little fingers: *īśānaḥ sarvavidyānāṃ śivaḥ*; *īśānāya namaḥ*; [with] the heart: *namo vaḥ kirikebhyaḥ*.

(l4. Homage to you, the Kirikas! Homage to the hearts, beginning with the Kirikas, to the hearts. "Homage to the Gaṇas"—this is for the back. Homage to the Gaṇas, homage to the back, homage to the Gaṇas. "Homage to the golden-armed one"—this is for the two sides. Homage to the golden-armed one, homage to the Lord of Beasts; homage to the golden-armed one on the two sides. "The unbent bow"—this is for the belly. The unbent bow, the mace; homage to the bow and so forth on the belly. "And he who is to be praised"—this is for the abdomen. And he who is to be praised, and he who is to be honored...

To Jātavedas, in the belly: *namaḥ* to Agni. With the mantra *hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*, at the navel: *hiraṇyagarbho yaḥ...* at the navel, *namaḥ* to Hiraṇyagarbha. With the mantra *mīḍhuṣṭama*, at the hips: *mīḍhuṣṭama... gahi*, at the hips, *namaḥ* to the most auspicious one (*śivatamāya*). With the mantra *ye bhūtānāmadhipatayaḥ*, at the private parts: *ye bhūtānāmadhi...* for us; *teṣāṃ...* we bow down; ...at the private parts, *namaḥ* to the lords of beings (*bhūtapatibhyaḥ*). With the mantra *ye anneṣu*, at the testicles: *ye anneṣu...* for them; *teṣāṃ...* we bow down.
To the testicles, homage to the Rudras! “O Jātavedas with the head... [is recited] over the anus. “Jātavedas with the head... the imperishable, supreme state, the highest head of the Vedas.

“To Jātavedas... [and] “The earth is the mother” [are recited] over the anus; homage to Jātavedas! “Do not harm our great ones... over the two thighs. “Do not harm our great ones... “Standing erect... “Homage to Rudra” [is recited] over the knees. “This one of yours, O Rudra... “This one of yours, O Rudra, clothed in skin” [is recited] over the knees; homage to Rudra! “The conqueror of the gathered... over the two feet. “The conqueror of the gathered... [is recited] over the feet.

To Soma, the measurer, [homage]. To him who has conquered through the union of the two shanks, homage. “The whole world” (viśvaṃ bhūtam)—thus [to the two] ankles. “May the whole world, the universe, be manifold”—thus [to the two ankles]. To Rudra, homage. “Those who on the paths” (ye pathām)—thus to the feet. “Those who on the paths... scatterers” (vyudhaḥ). To them, homage. To the feet. To the Rudras, homage. “He has spoken over, the one with superior armor” (adhyavocad adhivaktram).

“He has spoken over, the one with grain” (dhānyaḥ). Homage to the speech of the first consecration by the gods. “Homage to Bimbin” (namo bimbine)—thus the *upakavaca* (near-armor). “Homage to Bimbina and to Śrutasena.”

*Oṃ namo bimbādyupakavacāya namaḥ*. "Homage be to the blue-necked one" (*namo astu nīlagrīvāya*) is the third eye. "Homage be to the blue-necked one"—[this is] the hand; homage to the blue-necked one of the third eye. "Releasing the bow" (*pramuñcadhanvanaḥ*) is the weapon (*astra*). "Release... [and] "strike" (*vapa*); homage to the Blessed One, the Weapon. "Whoever there are so many... is the binding of the directions (*digbandha*). "Whoever there are so many... we know that."

Salutation to the Rudras from all directions. One should perform the placement of the salutation with "Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lord Rudra. Having placed the syllable *Oṃ* on the head: *Oṃ namaḥ* on the head; the syllable *na* at the tip of the nose; *nan namaḥ* at the tip of the nose; the syllable *mo* indeed on the forehead: *mon namaḥ* on the forehead; the syllable *bha* in the middle of the mouth: *bhaṃ namaḥ* in the middle of the mouth; the syllable *ga* in the region of the throat: *gaṃ namaḥ* in the region of the throat; one should place the syllable *va* in the heart: *vaṃ namaḥ* in the heart; the syllable *te* in the right hand: *teṃ namaḥ* in the right hand.

One should place the syllable *ru* on the left side: *ruṃ namaḥ* on the left hand. One should place the syllable *drā* at the region of the navel: *drāṃ namaḥ* at the navel. One should place the syllable *yā* on the feet: *...namaḥ* on the feet. Having placed *sadya* on the feet—namely *sadyojātaṃ vāya namaḥ* or *sadyojātāya namaḥ*—on the feet; and having placed *vāma* between the thighs—namely *vāmadevāya namaḥ*—on the thighs, one should place *aghora* at the heart: *aghorebhyo rūpebhyaḥ*; [thus] *aghora* at the heart.

*Namaḥ*. One should place *tatpuruṣa* on the face. From *tatpuruṣāya vidmahe* [to] *mukhe tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*. Having assigned *īśāna* to the head: *īśānassarvavidyānām* [to] *śivo me astu*. On the head, *īśāna*... he whose name is Sadāśiva. He who should say "Haṃsa, Haṃsa," he is named Haṃsa, Sadāśiva. Of this venerable Great Mantra of the Haṃsa-Gāyatrī: the Self (*ātman*) is the Seer (*ṛṣi*); the Unmanifest Gāyatrī is the Metre (*chandas*).

The Paramahaṃsa is the deity; *haṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*); *saḥ* is the power (*śakti*); *so'ham* is the pin (*kīlaka*). The application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining success through the grace of the Haṃsa-gāyatrī during recitation (*japa*). *Haṃ sāṃ* to the thumbs; *haṃ siṃ* to the index fingers; *haṃ sūṃ* to the middle fingers; *haṃ saiṃ* to the ring fingers; *haṃ sauṃ* to the little fingers; *haṃ saḥ* to the palms. Thus is the ritual placement of the limbs (*aṅgavinyāsa*). *Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvar-om*—thus is the binding of the directions (*digbandha*).

I behold that meditation which abides in going and coming yet is empty of going and so forth; it is incense and lamp, and the darkness of gloom. Standing within the midst of all people, I bow to that Swan, whose form is the Supreme Self.
The swans, the swans, the supreme swans—I am that swan.
May we know the swan, the swan; may we meditate upon the supreme swan. May He impel that swan for us.

Having thus performed the rite of placement (*nyāsa*), one should then begin the *saṃpuṭa* (encasement). Having placed the *saṃpuṭa*—consisting of the verses "trātāram indram," "tvanno agne," "sugaṃ naḥ panthām," "asunvantam," "tat tvā yāmi," "ā no niyudbhiḥ," "vayaṃ somam," "īśānam asme," "rudrāsyona," and "pṛthivī"—in the directions starting with the east and so forth; and having first uttered the *praṇava*, followed by the *vyāhṛtis* accompanied by the *praṇava*; and having fully uttered the seed-syllable (*bīja*) and the mantra, one should employ the seed-syllable at the end of the mantra, and then likewise the *praṇava* and the *vyāhṛtis*.

One should perform the *praṇava*: *oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ*. *Oṃ*, Indra is the protector; *tvam indraḥ*. *Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ*. *Oṃ*, obeisance to Indra in the eastern direction. *Oṃ bhūḥ... svaḥ*. *Oṃ*, "Do not [abandon] us, O Agni... *naṃ bhūḥ... svaḥ*. *Naṃ*, "Do not [abandon] us, O Agni... *naṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ*. *Oṃ*, obeisance to Agni in the south-eastern direction. *Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ*. *Oṃ*, "Make our path easy to traverse... *moṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ*.

Oṃ, in the southern direction, salutation to Yama. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ. Bhaṃ, may there be no [oblation] for those who do not press the Soma. Bhaṃ oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ. In the south-western direction, salutation to Nirṛti. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ. Gaṃ, I approach that... liberation. Gaṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ. Oṃ, in the western direction, salutation to Varuṇa.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ. Vaṃ, with our teams... ever-giving. Vaṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ. Oṃ, in the north-western direction, salutation to Vāyu. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ. Teṃ, we [go]...

Sāma: *aśīmahi*. Om Bhūḥ! To Kubera in the northern direction, obeisance. Om Bhūḥ! Ruṃ: We pray for protection to that Īśāna, the lord of all that moves and stands, the inspirer of the intellect; even as Pūṣan, may he be the guardian of our wealth, the protector who is undeceived, for our well-being. Ru Bhūḥ! Om! To Īśāna in the north-eastern direction, obeisance. Om Bhūḥ! Drāṃ: May the Rudras, the Maruts, and the mountains be with us in the slaying of Vṛtra—those many-invoked ones acting in harmony. He who...

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you have been established as the supreme among those who praise and exult. May the gods protect us; may they be our highest refuge. *Om bhūr bhuvaḥ*. *Om*, obeisance to Ākāśa. *Om bhūr bhuvaḥ*. To Yama:
"O Earth, be pleasant to us, free from thorns, providing a dwelling; grant us a secure and spacious place. *Om bhūr bhuvaḥ*. *Om*, obeisance to Pṛthivī.
In this very same manner, [one should perform the rites] within oneself.

On the forehead, the eyes, the ears, the mouth, the arms, and the nose; on the heart, the navel, and the head—these ten constitute the body on the two feet. (p29b, f27a, sideheading: *ātmasaṃpuṭīkaraṇam*, *raudrīkaraṇam*)

Oṃ bhūḥ | Trātā na indraḥ | Oṃ oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ | On the forehead: *indrāya namaḥ*. Oṃ oṃ bhūḥ | Naṃ tv agne 'smat | Naṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ | Naṃ on the eyes: *agnaye namaḥ*. Oṃ oṃ bhūḥ | Moṃ sugaṃ naḥ panthām | Moṃ bhūḥ | Oṃ on the throat: *yamāya namaḥ*. Oṃ bhūḥ | Bhaṃ asunvantam | Oṃ bhūḥ | Naḥ on the mouth: *niṛtaye namaḥ*. Oṃ bhūḥ | Gaṃ tat tvā yāmi | Moṣīḥ.

Gaṃ oṃ oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ | oṃ to Varuṇa on the two arms, namas. Om oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ | Vā... (l3) ...to Anila on the two thighs, namas. Vaṃ oṃ oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ | oṃ to Vāyu on the two nostrils, namas. Oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ | ...vayaṃ mahi | ... oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ | To Kubera on the heart, namas. Om oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ | Ruṃ to that Īśāna... ruṃ oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ | oṃ (l4) ...on the navel; to Īśāna, namas. Om oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ | Drām to us... O gods; drām.

Oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ. Oṃ, on the head: *namaḥ* to Ākāśa. Oṃ bhūḥ vaḥ. Yaṃ syonā prathāḥ. Yaṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ. Oṃ, on the feet: *namaḥ* to Pṛthivī. (L5. One should perform the Raudrī-karaṇa. One should install Rudra, accompanied by his seed-syllables (*bīja*), in the following locations: the crest-lock (*śikhā*), the head, the forehead (*phāla*), the eyes, the eyebrows, the mouth, the ears, the arms, the chest, the heart, the navel, the hips, the thighs, the knees, the shanks, and the feet. Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ. Aṃ: "Thou art the pervasive one (*vibhu*), the carrier away (*pravāhaṇa*); protect me with thy fierce aspect (*raudra-agni*), O Agni; carry me across."

Do not harm me! *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ*. To Rudra, salutation on the crest-lock (*śikhā*). *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ*. *Āṃ*, you are Vahni, the destroyer of obstacles; protect me with your fierce aspect, O Agni, carry me across, do not harm me! *Āṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ*. *Ā oṃ*, to Rudra, salutation on the head. *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ*. *Iṃ*, you are Śvātra, the wise one; [protect me] with your fierce aspect... *Iṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ*. *Oṃ oṃ*, to Rudra, salutation on the forehead. *Oṃ oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ*. *Īṃ*, you are Tutha, the knower of all...
Siḥ | Īm Om Oṃ Bhūḥ Vaḥ | Oṃ to the two eyes, obeisance to Rudra. Om Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Vaḥ | Um to the head, Taviro Suḥ.

Um Om Oṃ Bhūḥ Vaḥ | Oṃ to the eyebrows, obeisance to Rudra. Om Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Vaḥ | Ūm Aṅghārirasi Baṃ Bhārirau Siḥ. Ū Om Oṃ Bhūrbhuvaḥ Vaḥ | Ṛm Avasyurasi Duvasvān Raudre Siḥ. Ṛm Om Oṃ Bhūḥ Vaḥ | To the throat, obeisance to Rudra. Om Oṃ Bhūḥ Vaḥ.

*Vaḥ*. *Ṛṃ*, you are the ocean (*sindhu*), the purifier (*mārjālīya*), the wide one (*urau*). *Ṛm om oṃ bhū vaḥ*. Salutation to Rudra in the two arms. *Om oṃ bhū vaḥ*. *Ḷṃ*, you are the sovereign (*saṃrāj*), the one who dwells in the waters (*kṣayānu*), with the weapon of Rudra (*raudreṇāyudhena*). *Ḷm om oṃ bhū vaḥ*. *Om*, salutation to Rudra in the chest. *Om oṃ bhū vaḥ*. *Pariṣadyo’si pavamānorau siḥ*. *Ḷṃ om oṃ bhū vaḥ*. *Om*, salutation to Rudra in the heart. *Om oṃ bhū vaḥ*. *Eṃ*, you are the eastern wind (*prākvān nabhasvān*).

With *raudreṇa* [and] *siḥ*. *Em om oṃ bhū* [and] *vaḥ*. *Oṃ*, salutation to Rudra at the navel. *Om om oṃ bhū* [and] *vaḥ*. *Aim*, you are unsmeared, O purifier of oblations, *aurau* [and] *siḥ*. *Aim om oṃ bhū* [and] *vaḥ*. *Oṃ*, salutation to Rudra on the hips. *Om om oṃ bhū* [and] *vaḥ*. *Oṃ*, you are of true course, O auspicious one... from the beginning, *rau* [and] *siḥ*. *Om om oṃ bhūrbhu* [and] *vaḥ*. *Oṃ*, salutation to Rudra on the thighs. *Om om oṃ bhū* [and] *vaḥ*. *Auṃ*, you are the light of Brahman, possessing excellent luster, *mārau* [and] *siḥ*. *Auṃ*.

Oṃ oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ! Oṃ, salutations to Rudra at the knees. Oṃ oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ! Am, Ojas, [Śivasaṅkalpa], ekapād-raudre siḥ. Am oṃ oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ! At the shanks: salutations to Rudra. Oṃ oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ! Āḥ, you are Ahi, awakened; protect me with your fierce weapon, O Goddess, protect me, do not harm me! Aḥ oṃ oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ! Oṃ, salutations to Rudra at the feet. Thus.

Having performed the sixteen-limbed *raudrīkaraṇa*, one is liberated from all sins residing in the skin and bones. One becomes unconquerable among all beings. Then, let all disturbances caused by *bhūtas*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, *brahmarākṣasas*, *yakṣas*, messengers of Yama, *śākinīs*, *ḍākinīs*, serpents, wild beasts, thieves, and so forth, see me as blazing with light. Let them protect me. [One should recite] "The mind is the light, the unknowable; without fire, the head is the head" (*mano jyotir aboddhyaṃ niragnir mūrdhā mūrdhānam*) and "O Jātavedas, thy vital points" (*marmāṇi te jātavedaḥ*) upon the secret parts, the navel, the heart, the throat, the mouth, and the head. And with the mantra "The mind is the light, joined together" (*mano jyotiś ca yutena*).

Homage to Agni Jyotiṣmat in the secret place (*guhya*). "Agni has been awakened... (*abodhy agniḥ*)—homage to Agni in the navel (*nābhi*). "Agni is the head... (*agnir mūrdhā*)—he quickens; homage to Agni in the heart (*hṛdaya*). "The gods [made] the head of heaven... (*mūrdhānaṃ divo*)—homage to the gods in the throat (*kaṇṭha*). "The gods performed thy deeds... (*karmāṇi te*)—homage to the gods in the mouth (*mukha*). "O Jātavedas, accept... (*jātavedāḥ prati*)—homage to Jātavedas in the head (*śiras*). One should perform self-protection (*ātmarakṣā*). With the section beginning "Brahman created the self-endowed one" (*brahmātmanvadasṛjata*), [one says]: "Brahman created the self-endowed one—he who knows thus; homage to Brahman. Homage to Brahman.

The heart is the Śivasaṅkalpa: "By whom this past, present, and future world is entirely encompassed by the immortal; by whom the sacrifice with its seven priests is protected—may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve. (1)

May that mind of mine be of auspicious intent—the mind by which the wise perform their actions, from which speech and the mind proceed beautifully, and toward which living beings move in accordance with what is measured [by truth]. ||2||

That which the wise, weary of their works, perceive in the sacrifices and in the sacred recitations— that unprecedented power of the breathless one among living beings— may that be my mind, intent on auspicious resolve.

That which belongs to living beings, the splendor, the vitality, and the immortal light within creatures— that without which no action whatsoever is performed— may that be my mind, intent on auspicious resolve.
Like well-trained horses, O steed, we humans are led by you with auspicious reins; that which entered my heart, the most youthful one, as I moved—may that [be for me]... ||5||

In whom the Ṛg-verses, the Sāman-chants, and the Yajus-formulas [dwell]; in whom the reins shine as supports; in whom the entire consciousness and all delight of living beings abide—to him [be] praise! 6.
Whatever here is the sixth three-hundredfold secret abode of the sacrifice, its external name is nine; and that which is beyond, the ten and five three-hundreds—let him praise that. 7.
That divine power which goes far from the waking state, likewise goes far from the sleeping state; let us praise that one light, the far-reaching light of lights. 8.

By whom this universe was brought forth for the world, and by whom even the gods were born from the Great One, O Jātavedas; that which is Agni, the sole light within the darkness—to that we pay homage. 9.

By whom heaven, earth, and the intermediate space, as well as the mountains, the intermediate quarters, and the cardinal directions [are pervaded]—by him this world is pervaded; there is no other lord of creatures. 10.
Those who are the mind and the heart, those who are the gods, those who are the celestial waters, and those who are the rays of the sun—they move within the ear and the eye; may they protect us. 11.

May that which is inconceivable and immeasurable, which is beyond both the manifest and the unmanifest, which is subtle and subtler than the subtle—may that object of knowledge be praised by me! (12) One, ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, a hundred thousand, a million, ten million, a hundred million, a billion, ten billion, a hundred billion, a trillion, ten trillion, a hundred trillion, a quadrillion, ten quadrillion, a quintillion, and a sextillion—may those numbers be praised by me! (13)
Those which are five, fifteen, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, and a hundred thousand—those bricks of the fire-altar do not praise that body. 14.
I know this great Puruṣa, resplendent as the sun, beyond darkness. The wise perceive him as the source of the unborn. May that be my blessing. 15.
May he whom the wise sages purify, this very Brahman who has entered all beings—whether stationary or moving, the heavens, and the ether—be praised!
(16) That which is higher than the highest, and even beyond that which is beyond; that which is to be known as further than the furthest—that [Brahman] be praised! (17)
Brahman is higher than the highest; Hari is higher than that which is higher than the high. May He who is to be known as higher than the highest be praised. 18.
O Maheśvarī, that Gāyatrī who is all-pervading within the Vedas and other scriptures, consisting of the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāma, and Atharva—may she grant me [blessings]. 19.
I bow to that God Mahādeva, the supreme Puruṣottama, who is the syllable Om and whose essence is the Praṇava. ||20||
With self-restraint, one should praise that source, the syllable Om, the source, the Supreme Person, who is all and who is praised by all the Vedas.
(21) One should praise that which is recited in all the Vedas, the essence, the essence; for He is the bodiless, quality-less Self. (22)
O lotus-eyed one, may he who is honored with cattle, wealth, long life, [strength], progeny, and livestock—may he not praise you. 23.
May pride not harm me; may that [pride] be for my benefit. ||24||
O you who are honored by many, grant us long life; may that [protection] be ours. 25.
One may study the four Vedas and know all the Śāstras, yet one does not truly know the Itihāsas and Purāṇas. (26)
May that [deity] who dwells there in the beautiful peak of Kailāsa, the abode of Śiva, protect the gods; may that be mine. (27) Salutation to him who is in sleep and in fire; may that be mine. (28)
We worship Tryambaka; may he release me from death, not from immortality. 29.
I praise Virūpākṣa, who is the cosmic order and the truth. ||30||
Homage be to Kadrudra, the wise; let there be praise. (31) Homage be to the one who has eyes on all sides; let there be praise. (32)
The knowledge of Brahman, first born, has spread forth from the beginning. ||33||
He who is praised as the knower of the vital breaths in the piercing [of the heart]. ||34||
To him who is the giver of the self, we pay homage; may that be for me. 35.
May she whose door is fragrance bestow prosperity upon you. ||36||
Those Brahmins who always meditate upon this Śivasaṅkalpa shall go to the supreme liberation; may my mind be fixed on the Śivasaṅkalpa. 37.

*Hṛdaye śivāya namaḥ* (Salutation to Śiva in the heart). "By whom this [is pervaded]," "by whom the rites," "by whom the rites of the active ones," "that which is in the progeny," "the triplet," "that which is here the sixth," "that by which [they are] awake," "by whom this universe," "by whom heaven and earth," "those [who are] mind and the inconceivable heart"—in the *ekācaye* [hymn], and "I know this one," "of whom this," "the wise [know]," "beyond... and "...beyond the beyond," "Brahman," "he who indeed knows the God among the Vedas," "the *praṇava*, the syllable *oṃ*," "he who is in all," "being praised by the cows... "the great," "in *mānastoke*," the four Vedas.

The Rudra on the peak of Kailāsa; the *tryambaka* hymn; the *ṛta* and *satya*; the *kadrudrāya pracetase*; the *viśvatacakṣus*; the *brahmajajñānam*; the [verse] beginning with "yaḥ prāṇataḥ... ātmadā"; the *gandhadvārām*; and the *śivasaṅkalpa*: these constitute thirty-seven [verses].
The Puruṣasūkta is the head.

The Puruṣa with a thousand heads; the Sādhyas are the gods. Homage to Puruṣa on the head. The *Uttaranārāyaṇa* is the tuft (*śikhā*). "The god with a thousand heads... [the] lord of the voice. Homage to Nārāyaṇa on the tuft. The *Apratiratha* is the armor (*kavaca*): "May the swift one, sharpening his weapons, grant us protection. Homage to Indra as the armor. The two verses beginning with *bibhrāṭ* are for the eyes. For each person, there is the single-pot offering to Agni; the king [is he] whose hand holds the *pināka* bow and who is clothed in a skin. *Bibhrāṭ* for each person, for each person.

*vauṣaṭ* to the three eyes. *Tvam agne rudra*, known as the Śatarudriya, is the weapon (*astra*). "O Agni, you are Rudra; Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! To Rudra, the weapon, obeisance. Thus one should recite the five limbs (*pañcāṅga*) once. With the chest, the head, the gaze, the mind, and also with faith, as well as with the two feet, the two hands, and the throat—this is called the eight-limbed prostration (*aṣṭāṅga-praṇāma*).

"Hiraṇyagarbhaḥ yaḥ prāṇataḥ," "Brahmajajñānam," "Mahi dyauḥ upaśvāsaya," "Agninā," "Yā te agne imam," and "Yamaprastaram. With the words "Hiraṇyagarbha... vidhema," one should pay homage to Rudra with the chest. Thus it is everywhere. With "Yaḥ prāṇataḥ... vidhema," [one pays homage] with the head. With "Brahmajajñānam... vibhāt," [one pays homage] with the sight. With "Mahi dyauḥ... mabhiḥ," [one pays homage] with the mind. With "Upaśvāsaya... śatrūn," [one pays homage] with speech. With "Agninā... vidhema," [one pays homage] with the feet. With "Yā te agne... rūpāṇi," [one pays homage] with the limbs.

With the two hands: "imaṃ yama dādayasva" (give this to Yama); with the two ears: "iti" (thus). Having thus prostrated eight times, one should meditate upon oneself in the form of Śrī Rudra—resembling pure crystal, three-eyed, five-faced, ten-armed, adorned with all ornaments, with a beautiful blue throat, wearing a serpent as a sacred thread, decorated with serpent ornaments, and clad in an upper garment of tiger skin.

Holding a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*) and a rosary (*akṣasūtra*), bestowing the gestures of fearlessness and boons, with a trident in hand and blazing, possessing tawny matted locks and wearing a radiant topknot;
mounted upon the shoulders of a bull, bearing Umā as half of his body,
drenched in nectar, joyful, endowed with a divine form, joined by the deities of the quarters, and saluted by gods and demons.
He is eternal, everlasting, pure, firm, imperishable, and undecaying; he is the all-pervading Lord Rudra, who indeed possesses the universal form.

Having thus meditated upon Him who possesses form, the twice-born should then properly commence the sacrifice for the gods (*devayajana*). Of this great mantra, the *Śrī Rudrapraśna*: Aghora is the seer (*ṛṣi*); Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chanda*); that Sun, the Supreme Person, who is the very nature of the Saṅkarṣaṇa form, is the deity (*devatā*), namely Rudra; *namaḥ śivāya* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*);

*śivatarāya* is the power (*śakti*); *sadāśivāya* is the pin (*kīlaka*). For the sake of accomplishing my enjoyment and [other] goals, through the door of the propitiation of Śrī Sāmbasadāśiva, for the purpose of the consecration of Śiva (*śivābhiṣeka*).

The application (*viniyoga*): *Namaḥ* to the Self of the Agnihotra with both thumbs; *namaḥ* to the Self of the Darśapūrṇamāsa with both index fingers; *namaḥ* to the Self of the Cāturmāsya with both middle fingers;

*namaḥ* to the Self of the Nirūḍhapaśubandha with both ring fingers; *namaḥ* to the Self of the Agniṣṭoma with both little fingers; *namaḥ* to the Self who has performed [the sacrifice] one hundred and forty thousand times with both palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the ritual placement on the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*). The binding of the directions (*digbandha*) is: *bhūrbhuvassuvar om*. The meditation (*dhyāna*): (l5)
From the surface of the netherworld up to the vault of the sky, the self of the entire universe shines forth as a crystal liṅga;
from its crest, where the full moon gleams, it pours forth nectar.

A Brahmin, desiring the attainment of his desired goal, should constantly recite the Rudrānuvākas while performing a single *stokāpluta* [breath-retention] and meditating with rapid steps; he should then consecrate Śiva. Now, therefore, we shall explain the procedure for the ritual bath (*abhiṣeka*) of Rudra. Having bathed at the primordial sacred ford (*ādidevatīrtha*), one should bathe [the deity] within oneself with [the waters] that have risen. May Brahmā abide in the organ of generation.

May Viṣṇu abide in the two feet; may Hari abide in the two hands; may Indra abide in the two arms; may Agni abide in the belly; may [the Vasus] abide in the heart; may the Vasus abide in the throat; may Sarasvatī abide in the mouth; may Vāyu abide in the two nostrils; may the Moon and Sun abide in the two eyes. Being pure, self-restrained, a student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*), and wearing white garments—this is his sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). In the western region, his bones are facing that direction. May the Rudras abide in the forehead; may the Ādityas abide in the head; [may they abide] on the crown of the head.

May Mahādeva remain; may Vāmadeva remain at the crest-lock; may Pinākin remain at the back; may Śūlin remain in front; may the two hands remain as portions of Śiva on both sides; may the Winds remain everywhere. Then, outside, let all [deities] surrounded by garlands of flames of fire remain in all their respective places in every limb. May they protect me. Having wiped the limbs according to their characteristics with the mantra, "Agni is in my speech, heard" (*agnir me vāci śrutaḥ*), [one says]: "In Brahman"—thus regarding speech.

Having touched [them], he says: "Vāyu is my breath in the Brahman"—thus on the palms of the hands; "Sūrya is my sight in the Brahman"—thus on the eyes; "Candramas is my mind in the Brahman"—thus on the mind;

"The quarters are my hearing in the Brahman"—thus on the ears; "The waters are my semen in the Brahman"—thus on the generative organ; "The earth is my body in the Brahman"—thus on the body; "Plants and trees are my hair in the Brahman"—thus on the body hairs; "Indra is my strength in the Brahman"—thus on the arms; "Parjanya is my... [thus on the back].

*ṇi* on the head; *īśāno me manyau* (*ṇi*) on the forehead; *ātmā ma ātmani* (*ṇi*) on the heart; and again *punarma ātmā gopā* on all the limbs. Then, having removed the remains of the offering (*nirmālya*) with the *vyāhṛtis*, he offers water for libation (*tarpaṇa*) to the north, saying: "Salutation to Caṇḍeśvara. He then satisfies [the deities] with water: "I satisfy the god Bhava; I satisfy the god Śarva; I satisfy the god Īśāna; [I satisfy] Īśāna..."
I satisfy the god Deva; I satisfy the god Paśupati; I satisfy the god Rudra; I satisfy the god Ugra; I satisfy the god Bhīma; I satisfy the god Mahān.
Thus, "I satisfy; obeisance. Then he satisfies with water: I satisfy the god Bhava; I satisfy the god Śarva; I satisfy the god Īśāna; I satisfy the god Paśupati.

I satisfy [the deity]. I satisfy the god Rudra. I satisfy the god Ugra. I satisfy the god Bhīma. I satisfy the god Mahān. Having thus satisfied him, one should then worship him with offerings of unbroken rice (*akṣata*), flowers, incense, lamps, food-offerings (*naivedya*), betel-leaf, circumambulation, and prostration; then one should propitiate oneself [with the following]: "May I be propitiated by humans, by the Siddhas, gods, Asuras, and others.

I propitiate you with devotion; accept me, O Maheśvara. Having thus prayed and meditated upon the Three-Eyed One (*tryambaka*) with the mantra *tāt*, one should then invoke him with the mantra *ā tvā*.
"Let the bay horses, being of one mind, carry [thee] with white horses that possess banners; come quickly for my oblation, O Śarva, with those that are wind-swift, powerful, and as fleet as thought.

With this, I invoke Īśāna. "I take refuge in Sadyojāta"—with this, he offers a seat. "Salutation indeed to Sadyojāta"—with this, [he offers] water for the feet. "In every birth, O Bhava, do not transcend me, but favor me"—with this, [he offers] the arghya. "Salutation to Bhavodbhava"—with this, [he offers] water for rinsing the mouth. "Salutation to Vāmadeva"—with this, [he offers] the bath and the [five] limbs.

Bathing; "Salutation to Jyeṣṭha," thus [offering] a garment; "Salutation to Rudra," thus a sacred thread (*upavīta*); "Salutation to Kāla," thus perfume; "Salutation to Kalavikaraṇa," thus unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*);

"Salutation to Balavikaraṇa," thus flowers; "Salutation to Balapramathana," thus incense; "Salutation to Sarvabhūtadamana," thus a lamp; "Salutation to Manonmana," thus a lamp. At the proper time, the food offering (*naivedya*). Then he offers eight flowers with these eight mantras: "Oṃ, salutation to the god Bhava... to the great god... [and so on].

"Namaḥ"—with this [mantra], his Aghora-form stands before him. He should mutter the Rudra-Gāyatrī, "Aghorebhyaḥ tatpuruṣāya," ten times, a hundred times, a thousand times, or even more than that; then he invokes a blessing upon him. Then, pouring a continuous stream of water from a golden jar over his head—with milk, curd, ghee, honey, the juice of meat, sugarcane juice, coconut water, or scented water, or in its absence, with sweet water—he recites the Anuvāka beginning with "Śaṃ ca me" and "Namaste."

One should mutter one *anuvāka* from each of the eleven *anuvākas* beginning with "O Rudra, [your] wrath... and one *anuvāka* from each of the eleven *anuvākas* beginning with "O Agni and Viṣṇu, in harmony...".

(L5. One should perform the worship again for all [of these]. The subsequent worship should be performed by one desiring the destruction of sin, the destruction of disease, the desire for prosperity (*śrī*), the desire for peace (*śānti*), the desire for nourishment (*puṣṭi*), the desire for contentment, the desire for health, the desire for sons, the desire for food, the desire for sacrifice, or the seeker of liberation (*mokṣa*). Thus should the deity be worshipped. (P35a., F32b., Sideheading)

The ritual placement of the thirty-eight *kalās*. The teacher attains perfection (*siddhi*). He should give a cow with her calf, adorned with all ornaments; in its absence, he should give a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) according to his capacity—thus said the venerable Bodhāyana.
Then one should perform the fivefold Brahma-installation (*pañcabrahmanyāsa*).

"Īśāna of all sciences, Śiva..."—at the head: *īśānāya namaḥ*. "...to Tatpuruṣa, the giver of grace..."—at the mouth: *tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*. "...from the non-terrible ones, from the terrible ones..."—at the heart: *aghorāya namaḥ*. "To Vāmadeva, salutation"—at the secret place: *vāmadevāya namaḥ*. "...Sadyojāta, salutation"—at the feet: *sadyojātāya namaḥ*.
"Salutation to Sadyojāta. (L3. Thus, one should perform the placement sequentially with the fingers starting from the thumb and ending with the little finger.
[Then one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the thirty-eight kalās.]

Oṃ hoṃ, Īśāna, lord of all sciences; salutation to Śaśinī on the upper head. Oṃ hoṃ, Īśvara, lord of all beings; salutation to Aṅgadā on the eastern head. (L4) Oṃ hoṃ, Lord of Brahmā, supreme lord of Brahmā; salutation to Brahmeṣṭā on the southern head.
Oṃ hoṃ, may Śiva be mine; salutation to Marīcī. On the northern head. Oṃ hoṃ, Sadāśiva; salutation to Jvālinī. On the western head.
Oṃ heṃ, salutation to Avyaktakalā. On the upper face. (l5.)
Oṃ Heṃ, we know the Tatpuruṣa; salutation to Peace (Śānti) in the eastern face.
Oṃ Heṃ, may we meditate upon Mahādeva; salutation to Knowledge (Vidyā) in the southern face. Oṃ Heṃ, may that Rudra [grant us] stability (Pratiṣṭhā); salutation in the northern face.
Oṃ heṃ pracodayāt; homage to Nivṛtti at the western face.
Oṃ huṃ aghorebhyaḥ tamāyai namaḥ; homage to Tamā at the heart. Oṃ huṃ atha aghorebhyaḥ mohāyai namaḥ; homage to Mohā at the throat.
Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Ghorarakṣā; on the right shoulder. Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Aghoraniṣṭhā; on the left shoulder.
Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Sarvataḥśarvamṛtyu; at the navel. (l. 2)
Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Māyā for all [limbs]; at the belly. Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to you, Rudrabhayā; at the back. Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Jarā for all forms; at the chest.
Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva, obeisance to Rajā; at the secret place.
Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā, obeisance to Rakṣā; at the *liṅga*. Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Rudra, obeisance to Ratī; on the right thigh.
Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Kalā; obeisance to Pālī—on the left thigh.
Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Kalakāmā—on the right knee. Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to Vikaraṇā; obeisance to Saṃyamani—on the left knee. (L4)
Oṃ hiṃ, salutation to Balakriyā; on the right shank. Oṃ hiṃ, salutation to Vikaraṇa; salutation to Buddhi (Dhyai); on the left shank.
Oṃ hiṃ, salutation to Balakāryā; on the right buttock.
Oṃ hiṃ, homage to Pramathana, homage to Dhātrī—at the left hip.
Oṃ hiṃ, homage to Sarvabhūtadamana, homage to Bhrāmiṇī—at the waist. Oṃ hiṃ, homage to Manonmanī—at the right side.
(Oṃ hiṃ) Homage to Unmanā; homage to Bhavā. On the left side:
Oṃ haṃ, I take refuge in Sadyojāta; homage to Siddhi. On the right foot:
Oṃ haṃ, homage indeed to Sadyojāta; homage to Ṛddhi. On the left foot.
