O bird, speak auspiciously from every side; O bird, speak all that is holy for us. Speaking, O bird, speak what is auspicious; even when sitting silently, be mindful of our good fortune. When you utter your voice, let it be like the sound of a *karkarī* lute. May we speak aloud, winning great wealth and heroic sons. The gods generated divine speech; animals of every form speak it. May she grant us strength in pleasant songs.
May the cow Speech, yielding [milk], come to us with well-sounding praise. May auspicious deeds come to us from every side—deeds that are undeceivable and victorious.

May the gods, like kindled fires, increase our prosperity; may they be our protectors day by day. May the straight path of the gods be honored; may the chariot of the gods roll forth. We have approached the friendship of the gods; O gods, may you extend our life so that we may live. We invoke them first, whom we know, for the sake of greatness.

May Bhaga, Amitra, Aditi, Dakṣa, Śrī, and Madhu themselves [grant us fortune]. May Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, the Aśvins, and the auspicious Sarasvatī bring us well-being. May Vāta blow that healing medicine as a source of joy for us; may Mother Earth and Father Heaven grant it; may the pressing-stones that extract Soma grant it. O Aśvins, you bold ones, listen to this as a source of joy for us.
We pray to him, the Lord of all that moves and stands, the protector, to quicken us for our protection. May Pūṣan establish us in the increase of the Vedas.
May he whose life is consumed [by enemies], who is undeceived, protect us for our well-being! May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us prosperity; may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us prosperity;
may Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are unharmed, grant us prosperity; may Bṛhaspati grant us prosperity! The Maruts, with spotted horses, sons of Praśni, moving in splendor, hastening to the sacrifices;

they whose tongue is Agni, whose mind is the Sun, whose eye is the Sun—may all the gods come here for our protection! O gods, may we hear what is auspicious with our ears; O worshipful ones, may we see what is auspicious with our eyes.

With steadfast limbs and bodies, let us praise [the gods] so that we may attain the life-span ordained by the gods. O gods, a hundred autumns indeed lie before us, during which our bodies shall remain unharmed, and wherein sons shall prevail over their fathers. May you not harm our life in its middle course as it reaches its end. Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the mid-region; Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son. All the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is what has been born, Aditi is what is yet to be born. Firm is King Varuṇa, firm is the god Bṛhaspati; firm are you...
May Indra and Agni maintain the kingdom firmly, immovable like a mountain. Stand firm here like Indra; uphold the kingdom here;
trample down those who attack; let the enemies be beneath you. Stand like Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra. Thus ends the second chapter in the sequence of mantras beginning with *ṛkkilākārikā*.

[O King,] may she [the Grāhi] release him whom she has seized—whether he be one afflicted by unknown spirits or by consumption (*rājayakṣma*), or if indeed Grāhi has seized him—from that [affliction], through this oblation which is the giver of life.

This one, released by Indra and Agni—whether his life is exhausted or he has passed away, or even if he has been brought to the very presence of Death—I bring him back from the lap of Nirṛti. With the hundred-eyed oblation, which possesses a hundred autumns, I have rescued him for a hundred autumns. So that Indra may lead him across the furthest shore of all misfortune for a hundred autumns, live a hundred autumns increasing in strength; live a hundred winters, a hundred springs, and a hundred summers. May Indra, Agni, and Savitṛ [grant him] a hundred [years].

May Bṛhaspati restore this man with the hundred-lived oblation. I have brought you back; may they find you. You have returned, renewed. With all your limbs, may I find for you full sight and a full lifespan. O Vāyu, with warm water—may Aditi shave the hair. The sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*) is supreme and pure, that which was born together with Prajāpati in the beginning. Put on this bright, foremost, life-prolonging [thread]; let the *yajñopavīta* be your strength and splendor. O God Agni, giver of life, acknowledging old age, you whose path is clarified butter, who are anointed with clarified butter—[the clarified butter... *(Note: The final fragment "ghṛtam" appears to be the beginning of a further mantra or section.)*

Drinking the beautiful nectar of the cow, as a father supports his son with age, may you mount my stone-like seat; be firm like a rock. Overcome those who stretch out against you, along with those who stretch themselves out. The goddesses who spun, who wove, and who stretched the threads across the loom—may those goddesses clothe you for old age. Endowed with long life, put on this garment.

Bṛhaspati bestowed this upon King Soma as he was putting it on: "Go to your home, put on your own garment; be a protector from curses for those who seek your favor. Live a hundred autumns with great luster, and clothe yourself in prosperity. Put on this garment for well-being; be a protector from curses for those who call you 'bhūr'. Live a hundred autumns, O radiant one, and while living, distribute wealth among the noble. Driving away evil deeds, [be] the destroyer of the form of [evil] sound."

Again, [he ties it] three times... It brings strength through the out-breath and the in-breath; this girdle is dear to the gods, fortunate for me. Guardian of the *ṛta*, the further limit of ascetic heat (*tapas*), it strikes down the *rakṣas* and overcomes the enemy. Upon its back, all around... O girdle, may we not be separated from our auspicious husbands! You are the knot of the vital breaths; do not loosen!

The eye of Mitra, the supporter, powerful, resplendent, glorious, firm, and well-kindled; the slayer of the slayer, the garment of the decaying one—this victorious, unwasting skin I put on. You are Soma; make me a drinker of Soma, in whom the past and the future, all the worlds, are contained. With that [skin], I take hold of you; for myself I take hold of you; by Prajāpati I take hold of you. Devadattaśarman! I entrust you to the gods. To the Viśvedevas...

I entrust you to the deities; I entrust you to the All-gods; I entrust you to all [beings]; I entrust you to all [goddesses]. O you of good fame, make me one of good fame. As you are of good fame and renowned, so may I become one of good fame and renowned. As you, O god of good fame, are the guardian of the treasure of the gods, so may I become the guardian of the treasure of the Brahmins and of the Veda. We take away your first garment—may all [the gods] protect you.
May the gods rejoice! May many brothers and friends follow after this well-born one as he prospers. The Return Home.

I have fashioned this hymn for Jātavedas who deserves it, as one constructs a chariot, having fixed it within my own mind. For his providence is auspicious in the assembly; O Agni, in your friendship may I not suffer harm or waste away.

The triple life-span of Jamadagni, the triple life-span of Kaśyapa and Agastya; the triple life-span of the seers, that which is the triple life-span of the gods—may that triple life-span be mine. Be auspicious to me when touched. You are named "Razor"; the axe is your father; homage be to you, do not harm me. When you shave with the razor, when you shear with the shaver, when you trim my beard and hair, do not rob me of my face nor of my supreme life-span. (i) I loosen this bond of Varuṇa; I release it.

With this [formula], I seize away evil from the north for those who hate me; drive it away so that we may have food. May King Bhaga come to me; may they glide forth for my vigor and for good fortune. For the sake of distinguishing between gods and men, homage to Śāka and Jañjabha! Homage to those deities who are the seizers! That fragrance which is among the Apsarases, that glory which is among the Gandharvas, that divine and human fragrance—may it enter into me! O herb, you are the protector, the victorious, the powerful one.

May he make me full of essence like Soma and endowed with the splendor of the Sun; may he make me possessed of the luster of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcas*) and a consumer of food. You are free from the fetter. May this gold—which bestows long life, splendor, heroic vigor, and the increase of wealth—enter this victorious one for the sake of this fortune. I have indeed uttered the name of the gold as if it were that of my father. May it make me full of the splendor of Soma and the splendor of the Sun; may it make me a consumer of food. O high-flying, swift one, with a pleased nose, with the brilliance of a swan, the conqueror of wealth—may the serpents prosper together with him.

The supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*) that are concentrated in gold—Virāj, Svarāj, and Abhīrī who is in our house; the fortune (*lakṣmī*) that is at the head of the kingdom—such as that, we fashion for you. Bestow glory upon me among the Brāhmaṇas; bestow glory upon me among the kings. Glory among all the Śūdras—I am your glory. With the seasons, with the months of the year, and with their splendors, I follow after you. O *Śubhikā*, ascend my head and beautify my face. Beautify my face indeed, and may it become even more radiant.
Bestow fortune upon me! You whom Raṃyamadagni gave to Śraddhā for the sake of desire—may he release you for me for the sake of splendor and fortune.

When Agni has placed the people born of the triple womb above the wind, by that [power] may there be mountain-like splendor for both of us in this clarified butter within me. Your mind which has gone afar, look back at it in the mirror;

I see this here, not in myself: may there be long life and splendor for me. You are the sky, you are the earth; as a friend, protect me. You are the celestial, well-winged one; O soul of the intermediate space, guard me.

You are the Rathantara; you are the Bṛhat; you are the Vāmadevya. O Aśvins, let the chariot [protect] me; let the chariot not harm me; let it impel me with happiness. May they protect me equally; may they protect me equally. … I bring this offering to you. Make me the eldest, the sovereign lord. You are Soma; make me a drinker of Soma; make me worthy of homage; make me food. Destroy my evil. Brahman eats you. Thus ends the third chapter in the sequence of the *Ṛkkilakārikā* mantras.
May he, who rests upon the well-guided [chariot], be gracious toward us with his most excellent aids. O Indra, may he find pleasure in both [offerings] of ours; he bestows much of the Soma-juice.
May those straight-moving, non-leaping [steeds] bring us wealth, by which our friend, the driver, may choose what is desirable.

May Aryaman and Bhaga lead us together; O Gods, may lordship over the household be easy for us to control. Those sons of their own station, of wondrous deeds, have greatly stirred the two Mothers to first thought. And the truth of that which stands—

Of the world’s supporter, the son of the Lord, who dwells upon the two lotuses—those wise ones, masters of illusion, have measured out his kinship and common origin within the womb of the world. The poets, well-disposed, weave a new thread after a new thread in the sky and in the ocean; they are the teachers of the Sustainer of the Realm, like a bridge across the waters. May the Waters, when my feet are washed, destroy whoever hates me. In this family, may I possess the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*); may greatness be in me.
In me be fortune, in me be splendor, in me be glory; in me be sensory power and vigor. Come hither, O Āmā, and unite yourself with this glory and with this brilliance.

Make me beloved by all creatures and the lord of cattle. O Neṣṭṛ, I cut away that terrible form of yours; enter him with it who hates us and whom we hate. That which is the most excellent portion of honey, the supreme food and vigor—with that most excellent portion of honey, the supreme food and vigor, may I become the supreme eater of food.

Sweet are these [waters]. O Gaurī, you who have struck away evil, drive away sin, the evil of both myself and that person. Gaurī, worthy of being a cow, mother of the Rudras, daughter of the Vasus, sister of the Ādityas, the navel of immortality—I have spoken for the sake of the one seeking knowledge. Do not harm the innocent, the sinless Aditi. Drink the water; eat the grass. Om! Release her. She is the Virāj; may she not be harmed. May she bestow strength upon you. Om! Arrange her. You are the Virāj; as the Virāj, grant me food and heroic sons. The Virāj has been placed within me.
Place!
Desiring to conquer the world of Brahmā, I shall give to you, Śambhu, a maiden endowed with gold and adorned with golden ornaments.
O Viśvambhara, O witnesses of all beings, O deities of all,
I shall bestow this maiden for the deliverance of my sons.
A share is allotted but once; a daughter is given away but once;
and one says "I give" but once—these three things happen only once.
O Daughter, may you be before me; O Daughter, may you be at my side like a goddess;
O Daughter, may you be everywhere for me, so that through you as my wife, I may attain liberation.
O my own body, enter me; O your body, enter me.
Through this auspicious thread, which is the cause of the sustenance of those devoted [to you], may there be well-being.
I bind this upon your neck, O blessed one; live for a hundred autumns! O Varuṇa, grant it so that it does not kill my brother; O Bṛhaspati, grant it so that it makes me the wife of my husband.

O Indra, [drive away] the wife-killer and the ill-fortune from her with these [mantras]. O Savitṛ, may you grant her that which is not terrible-eyed, so that she may not be a killer of her husband, but devoted to her husbands.

May she be well-disposed and full of luster, a bringer of life and desirous of the gods; be one who brings no harm to our bipeds and quadrupeds. Here, I designate that ill-fortune of yours which is a killer of the husband.

You are Mitra. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of food—once. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of strength—twice. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of prosperity—four times. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of cattle—five times. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of the increase of wealth—six times. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of the seven priestly offices (*hotrā*)—seven times. We have become companions through the seven steps. May I attain your friendship. May I not be separated from your friendship. May you not be separated from my friendship. Let your heart be in my heart; let your mind be in my mind.

Listen to my words; be devoted to me alone. Be my companion, following me. Let your mind enter into mine; let your eye and your fortune be fixed on me. May all beings be in me; may your wisdom be centered in me. O sweet-smelling one, you who plunge into sweetness, whose tongue speaks honeyed words—place sweetness in my mouth. Sweetness has been made for me as a means of winning over;
this art of conciliation, the speech of a charmer, has been uttered. By that same charm by which the gods and Gandharvas were united, I touch your limbs.

May wind and water be beyond me; look upon me as you do the sun, and do not set your mind on others. Soma was the first to win her, Gandharva won her next; Agni is your third husband, and your fourth is born of men. Soma gave her to Gandharva; Gandharva gave her to me, together with wealth and sons; and now Agni has given this woman to me. O Sarasvatī, grant us protection, O blessed one, rich in strength! As such, we sing before you, the foremost of all that exists. I take your hand for the sake of noble offspring.

May I, with my husband, reach old age as he did. O Bhaga, Yama, Savitṛ, and the Purandhis—the gods have given you to me for the household. To Soma, who knows the wife; to Gandharva, who knows the wife; to Agni, who knows the wife. When the maiden, having looked upon the world of her husband, has been given over to the fathers, may she release herself from that bond. Loosened from there, may she make it well-fastened here. So that you may be rich in sons and fortunate here, [I] have bound you. Make me rich in sons and fortunate; may she have ten sons.
Bestow sons upon her; make her husband the eleventh. May Agni come first among the gods; may he release her progeny from the noose of death.

May King Varuṇa grant his approval for this, so that she, possessing sons and grandsons, shall not weep here in distress. May Agni Gārhapatya protect her; may he lead her progeny to a long life. May her lap never be empty; may she live as a mother and experience the joy of seeing her grandson. Let no cry of lamentation arise in her house at night; let her weep elsewhere than here.

Let them lie down. Do not, O Lord of the Locks, strike him who protects life; fall down! Shine forth upon the world, beholding the people with a well-disposed mind. Casting off childlessness, the death of a grandson, evil, or even affliction—like a snake shedding its slough—I cast the bond upon my enemies. I have ascended my own foundation; like a stone, may you be firm.
Tread upon those who stretch out against you; overcome those who stretch out against you. This woman speaks thus as she pours the parched grain into the fire: "May he be long-lived for me."
May the husband live for a hundred autumns. For you, O Agni, they have brought Sūryā in her bridal procession; O Agni, give the wife back to her husbands along with offspring.
Agni has given back the wife with long life and splendor; may her husband attain a full lifespan of a hundred autumns.
And with you, we shall overcome all enemies as one crosses deep waters with a boat. Thus, O radiant one, drive the chariot among the people to the sick man; the gods lead them back again to health.

From where they have come—may Pūṣan lead you from here by the hand; may the Aśvins carry you forward on their chariot to the house, so that you, O mistress of the house, being self-possessed, may ordain prosperity for us. I have ascended the path that is easy to traverse, uninjured, and a vehicle of well-being, upon which the hero does not perish and finds wealth among others. The herbs, the trees, the rivers, the grains, and the forests—O bride, may they release you, rich in offspring, from this place; may you be joyful. To the auspicious houses, with happy minds...

I take refuge in those who slay the enemy, the heroic ones, who carry nourishment for a long time and pour forth clarified butter; among them I lie down with a well-disposed mind. Here let cattle be born, here horses, here men; here let the abundance of wealth, accompanied by a thousand sacrificial fees, settle. You two become blue and red; when the *kṛtyā* (sorcery) exists, it is driven away. May your kinsmen prosper; let the husband be bound in bonds. You are firm, O you whose dwelling is firm; you are firm, established in firmness. Among the stars you are the pure one; protect me from the one who stretches out [against me] throughout the year.

The Seven Seers are fixed; their first name is Kṛttikā. When those who are firm bring forth the sixfold primary conjunction of the Kṛttikās, they kindle that which is our prosperity and the skill of Tvaṣṭṛ. O Aditi, grant us your approval! O Anumati, grant us your approval! O Sarasvatī, grant us your approval! O God Savitṛ, impel us! O Agni, you who are well-disposed, today kindle the fuel; producing the great, unconquered smoke, touch the divine summit with your rays and your flames.

Thereafter, for the Sun: "O Agni, you are the expiation of the gods... For Vāyu: "I, a Brāhmaṇa desiring a protector, take refuge in that body of yours which is the slayer of the husband, the slayer of offspring, the slayer of cattle, and the slayer of enemies; I make this [body] his. For Āditya: "The expiations of Vāyu, the expiations of Āditya, the expiation of Prajāpati. For Aryaman: "Let the fathers-in-law and the brothers-in-law quickly look toward the fire that has gone around [him]. O Prajāpati, I unite you with him like Surā with Sura."

May I become a lord of progeny, a lord of cattle; may I be possessed of offspring and possessed of cattle. Rise up, O Viśvāvasu! You take delight in the sacrifice. Seek another [woman] who is worthy of prosperity; unite with a husband in harmony. Rise up, O Viśvāvasu! For this woman belongs to her husband; Viśvāvasu, you have been praised with reverence and song. Seek another [woman]; she has been given to her husband. Know that his portion by birth is this house. For the sake of progeny, I take you. Men weep for the living, they are agitated at the sacrifice; they establish a long-lasting path of succession. The desirable wealth for the ancestors... which... This [gift] has been sent by me to my husbands, so that they may be released from their wives. O Lord of the Forest, just as you grow up firm with strength, possessing a hundred shoots, so may we grow up with our sons and cattle, possessing a thousand shoots, reaching the height of prosperity. O Lord of the Forest, just as you are fruit-bearing, so may I be fruitful through my sons and my cattle.
Rich in strength, rich in milk, swelling with milk—O Lord of the Forest, clothe us with milk! Behold this bride, she is auspicious; come together and look upon her.

Having bestowed good fortune upon her, depart to the setting [of the sun], O you who go astray. With minds bowed, with hearts submissive, with submissive navels, and with submissive bodies, may they bind you with the bond of desire for the sake of release. Those fetal spirits who have fallen away from us and dwell partaking of blood—to them, Svajā, *svadhā*, and homage! May they slumber and may they wake. Those who are raw, those who are unformed, and those who fall upon us satisfied—to them, Svajā, *svadhā*, and homage! May they slumber and may they wake. Those who belong to the child and those women...

To him who fashions all this—[to him] who, fashioned by the mind, fashions the mind; to him who fashions all this that is fashioned by the mind—to him [be homage]. To him who fashions that which is fashioned by old age—to him who fashions me—to him [be homage]. To him who fashions that which is fashioned by darkness—to him who fashions me—to him [be homage]. To him who fashions that which is fashioned by the ego—to him who fashions me—to him [be homage].

May *medhā* bestow upon me long life, may *medhā* bestow radiance, may *medhā* bestow progeny, may *medhā* bestow cattle. May my [progeny] not perish, may my cattle not be scattered. May the two males, Mitra and Varuṇa, [bestow] males.

O Aśvins, may both of you—the man Indra and the man Sūrya—cause me to prosper. You are the thunderbolt; homage be to you! Do not harm me. (…) O bird, you sing like a Sāman-chanting priest; you recite like a son of the Brahman at the Soma-pressings. May there be well-being for us, O bird; be well-disposed toward us.

Whatever misfortune, humiliation, slander, or reproach, whatever bad dream or ill-spoken word I have experienced—that I cast upon my enemies. Whatever has been encountered, whatever has been called out, or whatever ill-omened sound was made by birds...

Out of thirst for the deer, [it has bitten] those who are poisonous; homage to the Lord of dung, to Rudra! Homage to Rudra, the Lord of dung! You deserve the cow; let there be salutation to you, do not harm me. O Lord of Splendor, you have made a ford with a good watering place; standing as a pillar on the path, strike down evil intent. Those gods and divine beings who dwell in these trees, among the lords of the forest—may they carry prosperity and growth; may they not harm me. Carry away your indignation; let this pair [of opposites] depart from us; let this pair [be removed].

May this pair be rich in offspring; may this pair be rich in cattle; may this pair be rich in vigor. This great tree (vanaspati) has led you to well-being; may it lead you to prosperity. This hymn was spoken by Satyabhita; it is a Sūrya-hymn.
The earth was spoken by Satyabhita; it was spoken by Sūrya; it was spoken by the Adityas.
By the cosmic order, O Ādityas, Soma is established in heaven. ||1||
They harness the swelling, ruddy, and true one who stands around them; the luminous realms shine forth... 2.
In every endeavor, in every battle, we invoke you, the giver of wealth.
O friends, [sing] for the sake of Indra’s form. ||3||

The parrot, the parrot, the *śalmali* tree of universal form … | The vow, the well-wheeled chariot—ascend it, O bride, to the world of the Immortal; prepare a pleasant bridal procession for your husband. ||4||
They ascend the highest point and cast down those who stretch out against them.
Ascend the head of your husband and become a sovereign through your offspring. 5.
O Hero, be a sovereign queen; O Śr̥uvān, be a sovereign queen.
"Nānā"—be a sovereign queen; O sovereign queen, rule over the various directions.
With joy, the god Savitṛ has adorned the worlds, the creatures, and the sacred observances.

My lack of fortune was among women; my goat was among the *sumeka*s; my *vrātya* was among the *ītyā*s; my theft was among the Śūdra; my professional labor was among the Vaiśya; my knowledge was among the kinsmen of the Rājanya; my Brahman-murder was among the Naiṣāda; my killing of a Kṣatriya woman was among the *kuliṅga*s; my lewd dalliance was among the *ulala*s. My pride was among the *udīrṇa*s. What was my weeping among men? My burning was among the *dvipat*.

Upon the elephant is my leprosy; upon the dog is my skin-disease; among the Mlecchas is my discharge; among the Videhas is my consumption; among the Mahāvaṣyas are my ailments. O you who know evil! From the waters, may my sin depart; may the sacred word (*brahman*) drive away my guilt. For you, O Evil One, have been driven away again by us. Place evil in the world of the doer of good deeds—evil that has been cast off from us.
Having spoken against that evil which does not leave us, we abandon it elsewhere. May the thousand-eyed, immortal one [drive away] him who hates us; may he flee. Cast out that which we hate!

The goddess Medinī is the bearer of wealth (*vasundharā*); she has bestowed wealth upon us. He who is firm in his vows has extended his arms for the sake of the creatures of the world; you rule over the greatness of the great Unborn One. Savitṛ has thrice traversed the mid-air with his majesty; he has encompassed the three worlds and the three luminous spheres. He has passed beyond the three heavens, the earth, and the three [regions] with his threefold power. The serpent has established himself within the self by means of the three ghee-offerings. May fury be in the lion and the tiger; may it be within me [or between me and them]. May hunger be in the wolf and in the horse; may thirst be in the cloud, in the water, and in the desert. May weariness be in the royal palace; may stoniness be in me; may sloth be in the donkey.

In the hare is my doubt; in the horseless one is my trembling. In the tortoise is my bodily ailment; in the goat is my misfortune. In the beloved is my death; in the rival is my evil. In the companion is my Nirṛti; in ill-repute is my growth. In the axe is my prosperity; in the rhinoceros is my radiance; in the gayal is my wealth; in the white cow is my deafness. In the bear is my grief; in the monitor lizard is my sweat; in old age is my cold. In the black bird is my fear; in the donkey is my foul odor. In the owl is my...; in the *kyoka* is my envy; in the *utkaṭa* is my...
Difficult to overcome: the fish is my agitation; the frog is my delusion; the camel is my thirst; the deer is my fatigue;
the woolly sheep is my fragrance; the maiden is my ornament; the pig is my hunger; the female serpent is my sleep; the lightning is my pride; the leech is my moisture; the locust is my sin.

Now, O Goddess Vāsavi, you who possess the splendor of Brahman, you are the hearing, the eye, the fame, and the mind of the ancestors. You are the goddess who bears the Golden Embryo; you are the goddess whose belly gives birth. Sit upon this seat for the sake of truth. O Goddess who dwells in the ocean, who possesses the Sāvitrī, who takes away [evil], you are the earth held by me within my limbs. Greatly unassailable, you are the terrifying one at every peak and at every sacrifice. You are the wife of Indra, the pervasive, the fragrant one here, who surpasses the wind, who lies upon the waters, and who is herself the stream. O you whose food is truth, in the all-encompassing space, that enclosure is for the limb. O Great One, wife of Viṣṇu!

I bow to the goddess Mādhavī, beloved of Mādhava, to Lakṣmī, the dear friend, the goddess, the beloved of Acyuta. "Let us know the wielder of the bow; let us meditate upon the one who brings about the success of serpents; may Dharā inspire us. Thus ends the fifth chapter of the *Ṛkkilakārikānukrama*.
May Vāstoṣpati, the pillar, the weapon of the gentle ones, the breaker of the enemy, the eternal one—whatever fear exists, may Agni, the youngest, drive it away; may there be peace for us.

For the welfare of the subjects, for peace and prosperity, whatever [evil] has occurred in the trembling of the limbs or the movement of the heart; whatever has been uttered in a low voice or spoken aloud; whatever has been deficient or excessive; Agni, who is present among the various classes, [protects] from cattle, from bad dreams and evil dreams; from fear arising from the devouring of dreams or the sight of the impure—Agni [is our protector]. O Vāstoṣpati, be our furtherer; protect our household with cattle and horses, O Indu; may we be undecaying in your friendship. Be gracious toward us even for our sons; you are the dispeller of disease.

O Lord of the Dwelling, entering all forms... be auspicious to us who prosper. You are the sage, you are the seer; you, sustaining all forms, drive away the fear of the enemy army. Bestowing [blessings] upon the mother, supporting the foundation, and raising up prosperity, may he establish for us wealth, nourishment, and vigor. May death perish, may life increase; may death perish, may life increase, O Bhūḥ! May death perish, O Bhuvaḥ! May death perish, O Suvaḥ! Those fragrances, juices, colors, and strengths that are beneficial to us—may those waters be auspicious; may they carry forth our good deeds.

May those who are the nourishment, the great ones, and the dwellings of the gods—may they flow for me. May those at whose departure the entire world is born—may they flow for me. May those who are wisdom, the *sāman*-chants, and protected by splendor and glory—may they flow for me. May those wealthy waters that flow toward the south flow for me; may those wealthy waters that flow toward the west flow for me; may those divine waters that flow toward the north flow for me; may those wealthy waters that flow with nourishment flow for me. May those bright waters be auspicious for me, carrying my good deeds away. May the bay horses bring [the sacrifice] hither.

With a conscious mind, together with the white horses that possess banners, swift as the winds and endowed with powerful, delightful speed, come quickly for my oblation, O Śarva! These waters are auspicious, most auspicious; pure, most pure; [l6] holy, most holy; immortal, having the taste of nectar. May they accept these waters for washing the feet and for the guest-offering (*arghya*). Accept them, accept them, accept them; may the Blessed One Mahādeva accept them! These perfumes are beautiful, divine, adorned with all fragrances, purified by the *brahmapavitra*.

Purified by the rays of the sun, may this be accepted from you. These divine, auspicious garlands, adorned with every kind of flower, are purified by the *brahman*—may they be accepted from you. These divine, auspicious flowers, adorned with every kind of blossom, are purified by the *brahmapavitra* and by the rays [of the sun]—may they be accepted from you. This incense, endowed with the essence of the lord of the forest (*vanaspati*), is the supreme incense; it is to be smelled by all beings—may this incense be accepted from you. This light is Śakra and splendor, ever dear to the gods; it is the illumination of all beings.

"May this lamp be accepted. (L3. "We worship you—the one primordial, ancient Puruṣa, Rudra, Śiva, the creator of the universe... The wise one has driven away from the field the golden-toothed, pure-colored [beast], as he knows how. O inspired singer, by giving to him immortality, what have you done for us that is not beneficial, like Indra? 3.

The King of the fat has entered among the people; they have placed him here among mortals. May the sacred powers (*brahmāṇi*) release the curse upon him; may those who revile him become objects of revilement.

O Earth, that heart of yours which rests in the sky upon the moon—behold me, O wide one; may I not weep for the evil of a grandson. O Suṣimā, I know that heart of yours which is with Prajāpati; I know your mind. May I not weep for the evil of a grandson.
Let no Rākṣasa slay your son, nor let the cow stray, O mortal woman. May you be dear to wealth, prospering in your own home.

May the world-born, the one offered as the great oblation, the one who speaks the world—homage be to you, the all-born; Svāhā! May the Lord of the world-born, the General, the beloved of the peacock, the six-faced one, and the charcoal-colored one—through you may I [attain success];
homage be to you, bring me happiness; Svāhā! (2) (l6.

Subrahmaṇya, born of Rudra, born of Brahma, born of Bhū, born of Bhuvaḥ—svāhā to me for immortality! ||4||
To Subrahmaṇya, the progenitor of the world, the son of the Kṛttikās, the sixty-fold one, Svāhā!
(5) To him who is the progenitor of the world, whose speech is the progenitor of the world, the leader of Skanda and Viśākha, the one invoked with oblations, to the six-faced one, Svāhā! (6)

To the Ādityas, to the Viśve Devas, to the Sādhyas, to the gods, to the Ṛṣis, and to the Pitṛs—may winds of holy fragrance blow for you on the path; homage to those auspicious ones who bring pleasant sensations to the limbs. And where are the pleasant [winds] that bring pleasure to the flesh and pleasure to the bones? O Maruts, lead me to where the worlds of the righteous are. Homage to the great, homage to the small, homage to the young, and homage to the swift-moving. We sacrifice to the gods if we are able; may the gods accept our praise and the clarified butter. Agni... [iti]
"Ash-water," "the abode of ash," "the sky of ash"—ash indeed is everything. This ash is not [ordinary]; these eyes are ashes.

Whatever sin resides in my body, having entered the skin and bones, the consumption of the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) burns it away like fire consumes fuel. Truly, truly, let there be no more evil for us; let there be no more evil. Depart, O ancestors who have passed away! May you grant us well-being; we shall return again, just as a father [returns] to his son.

"May the friend see me, his friend, come. "In this way, may you other *preta*s who were previously moistened look upon him! "May these honey-sweet waters be milked for you in this world; may these honey-sweet waters be milked for you in the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*); may these honey-sweet waters be milked for you in the heavenly world (*svarga-loka*). "May my son live long, for the sake of longevity and splendor! O venerable and eternal deities who dwell in the cremation ground, [may you grant] that [longevity] to me from this place of action."

May they accept this offering, whether it remains or has been consumed. Grant us always the boon of long life, health, and what is dear to us. [Warding off] the defects of the *dṛkṣavāra* and so forth, and those born of phlegm, obeisance!
Obeisance to the deities, to the ancestors, and to the great yogins; obeisance, obeisance always to *Svadhā* and *Svāhā*. (Verse 4)
At the time of the śrāddha, having meditated upon Gayā, having meditated upon the Lord Janārdana,
and having meditated upon the ancestors beginning with the Vasus, the śrāddha ceremony is then performed.

May the dust from the feet of Brahmins purify me—those who are the causes for attaining all prosperity, who have arisen as comets to the destruction of their [evil] lineages, and who are bridges across the shoreless ocean of saṃsāra. May those dust-particles from the feet of Brahmins protect me—those who are like thousands of suns to the thick darkness of calamities, who are wish-fulfilling cows for the sake of accomplishing desired goals, and whose forms are as pure as the waters of all sacred fords (*tīrtha*). [They are] the remover of mental and physical ailments for men...

I bow to the lotus feet of the venerable Brahmins, which destroy death and poverty, and bestow prosperity, nourishment, and fame. By the mere sight of a multitude of Brahmins, the rays of sin are instantly destroyed; by saluting them, one gains auspiciousness, and by worshipping them, the imperishable state (*acyuta-pada*) is attained. O highly fortunate Viśvedevas of great power, may you come here! May you who are appointed to this *śrāddha* be attentive.
O ancestors, come from the celestial paths, from the oceans and the waters! In this sacrifice, may you obtain all desires; may you milk forth [the fruits] while they endure.

I take [this] from you for my father, grandfather, and great-grandfather. You are a balance, having Soma as your deity, measured by the cow... and the red [bull]. Come with the ancient ones, O ancient *svadhā*. Lead these fathers to the worlds; indeed, *svadhā* and homage! (L4) Struck down are the Asuras, the Rakṣases, and the Piśācas who dwell upon the earth! Let them go elsewhere, wherever their minds have gone. Come, O Fathers, gentle ones, with your deep, ancient lords, bestowing upon us progeny, wealth, long life, and a hundred autumns! (L5)

May those Fathers who are on earth, those who are in the intermediate space, those who are in heaven, and those who have become immortal, assemble at this sacrifice. With the waters that arise from the east and from the north—with those waters which are the sustainers of the entire world—I place a barrier between [the living and] the Fathers; *svadhā*, homage! (L6) I have placed a barrier with the mountains, with the great earth, with the sky, and with the boundless protective powers; I place a barrier between [the living and] the Grandfathers; *svadhā*, homage! I have placed a barrier with all the seasons, with days and nights along with their junctions, and with the half-months.

Within the months, the father has established an interval; *svadhā*, obeisance! That which my mother, wandering and unfaithful, caused me to lose—may my father take that seed back for me; let no other come near me. O Fathers, *svadhā*, obeisance! That which went to the flesh-eaters, that which led away to the worlds, that which the Knower of Beings (*Jātavedas*) carried off—that I cause to enter you again. Unharmed, be united with all your limbs. O Fathers, *svadhā*, obeisance! To Soma accompanied by the Fathers, we offer this oblation to the powerful one; [we offer] this strength.

Enjoy the oblation; [O Agni,] you who are self-born, [offer it] to the gods and the ancestors—*svadhā*, homage! I invoke Yama, accompanied by the Aṅgirases for our protection and accompanied by the Pitṛs. O Vaivasvata, this food is yours; [O Agni,] you who are self-born, offer the oblation to the gods and the ancestors—*svadhā*, homage! Since you, O Kavyavāhana, increase the sacrifice and honor the Pitṛs, carry the oblation to the gods and the *kavya* to the Pitṛs—[O Agni,] you who are self-born, [offer it] to the gods and the Pitṛs—*svadhā*, homage! The earth is your vessel, the sky is the lid; through the mouth of Brahman, I offer you.

I offer you into the out-breath and in-breath of the learned Brāhmaṇas; you are imperishable. Do not be exhausted for me in yonder world, in that world. The earth is your body; Agni is seen as your form; the *ṛg*-verses are your majesty. The intermediate space is your body; Vāyu is seen as your form; we delight in your majesty. The sky is your body; Āditya is your illuminator; the *sāman*-chants are your majesty. Viṣṇu alone is the great being, who, as the self of beings, pervades the three worlds and has become manifoldly divided.

He who enjoys all is Viśvabhuja, free from decay. For the sake of the liberation of my ancestors, I perpetually bow to the feet of Īśāna, Viṣṇu, the Lotus-seated One (Brahmā), Kārttikeya, and the triad of fires; to Karaja, Niśa, and Gaṇeśvara; and to Krauñca, Amarendra, Kalashodbhava, and Kāśyapa. (Verse 2) To those gods who are without a portion and excluded from the sacrificial distribution, I shall offer food—the scattered oblation for the Vaiśvadeva rite. To those who are unrefined, those who have passed away, and those women of the family who were abandoned, I shall give the scattered food.

And from them [comes] that which pertains to the ancestors. Without doubt, Viṣṇu is the imperishable means to liberation. May the scattered food—the most excellent and supreme offering for the ancestors—be for those who are Vaiṣṇavas, those in my lineage who have been cremated by fire and those who have not yet been cremated. May they be satisfied by what is given upon the earth; and when they are satisfied, may they attain the supreme goal. To the deities, to the ancestors, and to the great yogis, [I offer] salutations, to Svadhā and Svāhā; always, salutation after salutation. May our donors increase, and may the Vedic lineage alone flourish for us. Faith...

And may it not depart from us; may we have much to give. May your donors increase, O ancestors; may there be faith for you. May food be abundant for you, and may we indeed obtain guests. May we have both those who cross over [to us] and those who do not, and may we have neither those who cause distress nor those who are hostile. May you receive what is offered to you; may there be those who ask of you, and may there be none who asks of us. Rest, O ancestors; bestow upon us, O ancestors, an embryo—a boy adorned with a lotus wreath—just as here...
"Punīṣa sṛgiti. Thus ends the seventh chapter in the sequence of the *Ṛkkilakārikā* mantras. 7.

The Vedas are your heads; the syllable (*akṣara*) is your supreme station. The head of the Vedas is the highest. To Jātavedas, Mother Earth [belongs]; may the Rudras, the bountiful ones, [be] with us in the slaying of Vṛtra, O you who are invoked by many;

may he enjoy [it]. May there be well-being for you; let it be established for the wielder of the thunderbolt. May the gods, with Indra as their chief, protect us. Be pleasant, O Earth, thornless and a place of rest;
grant us wide protection. To Jātavedas: by day you are the purifier; whether you are Vaiśvānara or the lightning of the sky, bring peace to all creatures.

Bestowing a world, a wave of abundance, and prosperity upon the sacrificer, turn toward us. That by which this past, present, and future is entirely encompassed by the immortal, that by which the seven-priest sacrifice is protected—may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent. That by which the wise perform their rites, from which they proceed with speech and mind toward what is beautiful, that which living beings follow in accordance with its measure—may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent. That by which the skillful and wise perform their works in the sacrifice during the established ordinances—may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent.

Whatever consumption (*yakṣma*) is unprecedented within living beings, may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent (*śivasaṅkalpa*). Whatever wisdom, brilliance, and fortitude there is, and whatever immortal light is within living beings—that without which no ritual action whatsoever is performed—may that be mine. O swift one, may we [attain] horses and cattle; O steed, may we [attain] men through thy well-directed, beautiful powers. That which is most ancient, entered into the heart, and most youthful—may that be mine. In whom the *ṛc*s, *sāman*s, and *yajus* reside, in whom the tethering-ropes find their foundation.

The burdens shine; that in which the mind of all creatures finds every delight—may that be mine. That which here is the sixth, the three hundred, the secret body of the sacrifice, the ninefold external name;

that which is beyond the thirty-five and ten—may that be mine. "May the divine [state] of the waking one go far away, and likewise that of the sleeping one. O you who go afar, the one light by means of light—may that be mine.

By whom this entire world of moving beings came into being, and the gods who are born from the Great One, Jātavedas; those gods who are the light from out of darkness—may that be mine. By whom the sky and the earth...

The atmosphere, the mountains, and those that are the intermediate and cardinal directions—by these this world is pervaded; that [Self] of mine which belongs to all creatures. Those who are the mind and the heart, and the gods, and the celestial waters, and the rays of the sun—they move within my hearing and my sight; that [Self] of mine. That which is inconceivable and immeasurable, which is beyond the manifest and the unmanifest, subtle and subtler than the subtle, the object of knowledge—that [Self] of mine.
Those which are five, fifteen, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, and a hundred million—they are the fire-altar bricks; that body of mine, which the wise purify.

The sages [worship] Brahmā, who is bowed down to by the moon; the stationary and the moving, the sky, and space—may that be mine. That which is higher than the highest, and even higher than that, and whatever is beyond—that which is to be known as higher than the highest—may that be mine. The Gāyatrī, who is at the beginning of the Vedas, the all-pervading Maheśvarī, together with the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāman, and Atharva [Vedas]—may that be mine. The self-restrained [one worships] the Praṇava, the syllable Om; the Praṇava is the Supreme Person (*puruṣottama*). He who... together with the Vedas—may that be mine. He who [worships] the God Mahādeva, the supreme, the most excellent, the syllable Om—may that be mine.

That which is the self of the *praṇava*, which is recited throughout the years and in the Vedas as the Lord of Speech—that formless, quality-less Self, may that be mine. That which is cherished by cows, by wealth, by strength, by progeny, and by cattle—the lotus-eyed one, may that be mine. He who has studied the four Vedas and the various sciences, and who knows the Itihāsas and Purāṇas—may that be mine.
On the beautiful peak of Kailāsa, in the auspicious abode of Śaṅkara, where the deities rejoice—may that be mine. Those Brahmins who always meditate upon this *Śivasaṅkalpa*...

They shall go to the supreme liberation; that is mine. For he is the one who possesses the power, the good archer, who rules over every healing medicine. We honor him with our minds, O Rudra, the divine Asura; we serve him with salutations. May he be my lord, may he be my most exalted lord; may he be my possessor of all medicines, he whose touch is auspicious. Truly, in the binding of strength, he is the skillful one; like Indra, he bestows strength upon us. Strength for our children and grandchildren so that they may live—you indeed are the giver of strength, born for glory, for the attainment of prosperity.

He bestows prosperity and vitality upon the progenitors; through the ridge [of the altar], they attain prosperity and immortality, becoming true, self-existent, and of unchanging form. The gift of stones is for the sake of prosperity.

First, there is the invocation from the east, and therein the performance of salutation (*namaskāra*). Then one should perform the offering of water (*arghya*), as well as the prayer, the formal permission, the ritual bath (*snāna*), and the libation (*tarpaṇa*).
The Gift of Stone:
"O Kṛtyā, who has arisen from the *pippala* tree and causes terror to the world, this stone is given by me to you as a provision for your food. (l. 2)
Invocation:
O Viśvācī and Ghṛtācī, O source of all, O Lord of the people!
O God, grant your presence to me here in the salt-water ocean.
Homage:
salutations to you, the protector of the universe; homage to Viṣṇu, the lord of the waters. Homage to him who has the form of the ocean; homage to the lord of the rivers.
Salutation to the ocean, to Vāyu, to the lord of the rivers;
salutation to the father of all streams, to Viśvakarman who manifests in many forms.
Every day, the mortal [offers] the oblation;
[he offers] the guest-offering (arghya)— glorious, consisting of all jewels, with hands that are mines of all jewels.
O Great Ocean, you who are the preeminent among all jewels, accept this water offering.
O Great Ocean, you who have entered all the sacred fords (*tīrtha*) upon the earth:
grant me the fruit of my bath; protect me from everything by your power.
"O Lord, grant me permission to resort to your sacred fords— permission from you, whose mouth has terrifying fangs and whose teeth are bared in a gaping maw."
O you of exceedingly cruel and massive body, resembling the fire at the end of an eon;
homage to you, Bhairava! You should deign to grant me permission.
The bath is the source of the Vedas and other sciences; the Lord of Rivers is the source of the ocean’s jewels;
Agni is your splendor, and Iḍā is your splendor; Viṣṇu, the bestower of seed, is the abode of immortality.
I offer this water to you, distinct from those other waters which enter the Kāñcī and the Sindhu;
like a snake casting off its old skin, I cast away evil from my body, approaching you with my head bowed.
The libation (tarpaṇa):
[one should offer it] to Pippalādi, Kavikaṇva, Kṛtānta, Jīviteśvara, Manyu, Kālarātri, and the Lord of the Hosts of Days (Ahargaṇeśvara). (Verse 3)
Regarding the "field-gathering" (kṣetrapiṇḍa): from Brahmā down, those born in my paternal lineage, as well as those born in my maternal lineage,
and all those who are my slaves in these two lineages, as well as my dependents, servants, friends, and companions— [all these belong to me].

To the animals and trees that have been touched or seen by me, and those who have rendered me assistance, and those with whom I was associated in other births—to them I offer this *svadhā* and the funeral rice-ball (*piṇḍa*). (1)
Those who have died in my paternal lineage and likewise in my maternal lineage;

those who have died among my teachers, fathers-in-law, and kinsmen, as well as other relatives; those in my family whose sacred marks have been lost, and those deprived of sons and wives—[for all these may this merit be].
Those who have been struck down by the omission of ritual acts, those born blind, those who are lame,
those who are deformed, and those who were miscarried— whether they were known or unknown in my family—
may this *puṇḍra* offered by me reach them imperishably.
In the terrible Asipatravana, in Kumbhīpāka, and in Raurava;
For the sake of their deliverance, I offer this funeral ball (piṇḍa);
for those whose lineage has perished, there is indeed no giver within their family. 3.
May this gift of Dharma, bestowed by me, remain inexhaustible. (4) May it reach all beings from Brahmā down to a blade of grass—the gods, sages, ancestors, and humans.
May all the ancestors—the mothers, maternal grandfathers, and the rest—be satisfied;
as well as those of the ten million past lineages dwelling throughout the seven continents.
May this water with sesame seeds reach as far as the world of Brahmā;
whatever exists, moving or unmoving, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass.
May my ancestors, whoever they may be who exist in the form of pretas, attain satisfaction through the water offered by me.
May they all attain satisfaction through these water-libations mixed with sesame seeds and touched by *kuśa* grass. (L4.
[Thus ends the eighth chapter in the sequence of mantras for the *Ṛkkilakārikā*.]

Those who, through sacrifice and the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), attained companionship with Indra and immortality—to them, O Aṅgirases, may there be prosperity! Accept this descendant of Manu, O wise ones.

Those who by means of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*) caused the Sun to ascend to heaven, spreading out the Earth, the Mother—O Aṅgirases, may there be good progeny for you! Accept this descendant of Manu, O wise ones. This one, at the very center, speaks most sweetly in your house; O divine sons and seers, listen to that!

O Aṅgirases, let there be the Subrahmaṇyā for you; may the son of Manu accept us, O wise ones. O Virūpas, you Ṛṣis of profound inspiration, those Aṅgirases who were born from Agni—those Aṅgirases who were born from Agni, the Virūpas from heaven—they have driven away the people, the eternal darkness of the Aṅgirases.

He bestows gifts upon the gods. With Indra as their ally, they released the wealth, the cattle-rich, horse-filled [booty] from Vṛtra. Giving to me a thousand [cows], the Aṣṭakas and the Agrus [have been satisfied].

Or may we be born among the gods as those who have performed [sacrifices]. In the *manastoma*, let there be praise for him who gives a thousand [cows] with a hundred horses to the one who is in need. No one indeed sinks into distress. Like the sky, that support of the world, that sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) of the praiseworthy one has spread out and increased like the poles of a chariot. From here, O Dāsas, we have bestowed wealth upon the giver. Whatever is desired, let us offer it. May the leader of the village, the Maruts, and the mind be victorious; may the sacrificial fee bring the sun. Let that [fee] play, O Gods; let Vāyu move forth.

"In that [sacrifice] where they, unwearied, win the prize—food upon food he offers; he offers everything. It is known [from scripture]: 'For the attainment of all, for the securing of all, for the acquisition of all.

Thus, in the midday pressing and the third pressing, the eightfold, the ninefold, the twenty-sevenfold, and the thirty-threefold [Stomas] are excluded. The Atirātra with all the Prṣṭhas is the tenth day. The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) at this time is such that the Brāhmaṇas have not seen its like; it places the person well-established and well-provided. Just as in the Aśvamedha, those who fasten the girth-strap (*yoktra*) or the horse's bit, for her [the wife], he [the Adhvaryu] [takes] from the girth-strap."

He brings forward a full vessel. While it is being brought, he mutters: "May you be united with long life and progeny. Having led her away, having wiped her face, they rise. [The bride says: "May I be one who possesses nourishment, cattle, offspring, and householdership. May you not be a widow for more than a hundred years, O lady of good vows; may you be radiant, a lawful wife, and devoted to your husband."

May you give birth to many sons and never experience suffering anywhere. May your husband always be a drinker of Soma and devoted to righteousness; may you have eight sons, be very prolific, fortunate, and faithful to your husband.
She was always blameless toward both her husband and her father’s brother,
just as Indrāṇī is to Indra, Śrī to Śrīdhara,
and Gaurī to Śaṅkara— so too was she toward her husband.
Bṛhaspati is so called because he is the nourisher of the firm (dhruva) weapons and because he is great (mahat).
May Prajāpati, through me as his consort, cause him to live for a hundred autumns;
may Tvaṣṭṛ generate you as her offspring, and may Tvaṣṭṛ make you her husband.
May Tvaṣṭṛ grant me a long life of a thousand years.

May he make me glorious, powerful, and sovereign; may he become the king and overlord of men, a lord of horses whose passion is manifold, and one of auspicious limbs. Granting offspring and wealth here, O you who desire sons for your own progeny, I beheld you with my mind as you were conscious, born of austerity, emerged from darkness. I beheld you with my mind.

Meditating, with well-established bodies, at the proper season, she who is in need approaches; the young woman becomes manifest for the sake of progeny through her own offspring, O you who desire a son. One should bestow a thousand upon the reciter, a hundred upon the preparers, and likewise upon the one who wears [the garment].
A white horse, a white chariot—may the Hotṛ proclaim this for one desiring a son; for they indeed obtain sons. *Svāhā*! For the expiation of sin committed against the gods, we are born;
*svāhā*! For the expiation of sin committed against men, we are born; *svāhā*! For the expiation of sin committed against the ancestors, we are born; *svāhā*!

You are the expiation for the sin committed by oneself; *svāhā*. You are the expiation for whatever sin has been committed by him by day and by night; *svāhā*. You are the expiation for whatever sin we have committed while sleeping or waking; *svāhā*. You are the expiation for whatever sin we have committed knowingly or unknowingly; *svāhā*. For each [sin] by which [it was committed], you are the expiation; *svāhā*. Protect us from sin, O Agni; *svāhā*. Thus [the offerings] beginning with the five *bhūḥ* etc., and four [beginning with] *agnaye svāhā*, *somāya svāhā*, *dhruvāya*...

To Dhruva, the terrestrial one, svāhā! To Dhruvakṣiti, to Acyutakṣiti; to Īśāna, to Jayanta, to Ruci, to Dharmaruci, to Dhanvantari, to Vidyā, to Ambikā, to Hari, to the Gaṇas, to the Gaṇapatis, to the Assemblies, to the Viśvedevas, to the Sādhyas, to all the gods, to all the deities; to the four [worlds] beginning with Bhūḥ; to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā! To Dharma, to Adharma, to Kadru, to the mother of the Nāgas, to the serpents, svāhā! To the goddess Acalā.
Svāhā! To Vāstupālī together with her retinue, to the Waters, to Varuṇa, to Prajāpati, Svāhā! To Parameṣṭhin, Svāhā! To the Seers, to Rudra, to Rudrāṇī. ||9||1||
To the herbs and forest trees; to the Rakṣas and the divine folk; to Kāma, Bhaga, and Śrī; to Viṣṇu and Graha; to the King of Grahas. ||8||2|| To wealth and grain;

to Vaiśravaṇa; to Śrī and Puṣṭi; to the mortar and pestle; to the lower and upper grinding stones; to Samūhinī, to the gods—Svāhā! ||7||3|| To the Grahas; to the endings; to the lords of the endings; to the Sarpas and the divine folk; to all beings; to the intermediate space; to that which is not the intermediate space; to Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ. ||6||

4. For prosperity; for abundant prosperity; for that which moves and that which wanders in the world, for Bhaga who acts through desire, for him whose name is [Bhaga], Svāhā! To the two eldest; to the two youngest; to the two hands; to Śrī; to Viṣṇu; to Rudra; to the cattle; to Paśupati. 10.5. To Vāstoṣpati; to the Earth; to the intermediate space; to the Sky; to Sūrya; to Candramas; to the constellations; to the waters; to the plants; to the lords of the forest. 10.6. To the moving and the unmoving; to those that float; to the serpents; to the regions.

To the *kalās* (time-units), to the worlds (*lokās*), to the Vedas, to the *ṛṣis*. || 8/7 || To the *vasus*, to the *rudras*, to the *ādityas*, to Indra, to Bṛhaspati, to Prajāpati, to Brahman—*svāhā*! || 8/7 || To the ancestors (*pitṛs*), *svadhā*, obeisance, *svāhā*! To the grandfathers (*pitāmahās*), to the great-grandfathers (*prapitāmahās*). Obeisance to the Lord Rudra. To the eastern direction, to the southern direction, to the western direction, to the northern direction, to the upward direction, to the downward direction. To Yama, to Nirṛti, to the *rakṣases*, to Īśāna—to those who... || 8/8 ||
The beings roam by day and by night, seeking offerings, the servants of the fleeing Rudra. To them I bring an offering, desiring prosperity;
may the Lord of Prosperity bestow prosperity upon me, svāhā! Homage to Rudra, the earthly one, svāhā! To the gods, svāhā! To the ancestors, svadhā, homage, svāhā!
To the beings, svāhā! To human beings, svāhā! To the Brahmins, svāhā! And to the two dogs, the dark and the brindled...
Born in the lineage of Vaivasvata, I shall grant a *puṇḍra* to those two; let them indeed be non-violent.
May the crows belonging to Indra, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Soma, Yama,
and Nirṛti accept the ball of rice offered by me upon the ground.

The Vedas, humans, animals, birds, Siddhas, Yakṣas, Uragas, hosts of Daityas, Pretas, Piśācas, and all trees—those who desire food, [may it be] given by me. Thus ends the ninth chapter in the sequence of the Ṛk-kīlaka-mantras. (l2.
The Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas and others, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Guhyakas.
O deities, all sages, and likewise the lords of the hosts, I cast this suspicion outside; therefore, go far away!
May there be longevity, strength, fame, splendor, progeny, cattle, and wealth.
O Lord of the Forest, grant us Brahman-knowledge, wisdom, and intelligence.
Whether one is impure or pure, or has fallen into any state whatsoever,
whoever remembers the Lord Īśāna together with Ambā is pure both internally and externally.
The sin accumulated through mind, speech,
and ear is undoubtedly dispelled by the very sound of Śrī Śiva’s name.
Tithi is Śambhu, likewise the day of the week is Śambhu, and the lunar mansion is indeed Śambhu as well.
Yoga and the instruments of action—the entire world is composed of Śambhu;
you who possess the forms of all deities, both the celestial and the earthly waters, I bow to you and shall bathe in you for the sake of complete purification. (L5)
Salutation to Him whose hair consists of clouds, whose every limb and joint contains the rivers, and whose belly holds the oceans— to that Self of Water,
the support of the entire universe, who bears the conch, the discus, and the mace.
"O Lord, grant me permission to resort to your sacred ford.
Homage to you, Bhairava, who are exceedingly fierce, possessed of a massive body, and resemble the fire at the end of an aeon; you ought to grant me your leave."
May the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, the oceans,
lakes, streams, ponds, and other sacred bathing places (tīrthas) be present for me at the time of my bath.

Let Mahādeva be worshipped—the Lord of the Universe, the destroyer of Tripura, Śrīkaṇṭha, Merukodaṇḍa, Hara, the fierce remover of sins. O Urjāvahantī, satisfy my ancestors with nectar, clarified butter, honey, milk, kīlāla, distilled liquor, and svadhā; may they be satisfied, may they be satisfied! Om, salutations to Brahman, salutations!
Let there be obeisance to Agni, obeisance to the Earth. Obeisance to the plants; obeisance to Speech; obeisance to the Lord of Speech; obeisance to the Great Viṣṇu, I perform [this].
Whatever water has been defiled by the accumulation of bodily impurities—for the sake of purifying the sin thereof, I satiate Yakṣman.
"Whatever members born in my family, whether belonging to my lineage or not, who have died childless—
may they accept this water from the wringing out of my garment, which has been given by me."
The supreme light, the root of all, higher than the highest,
residing in the hearts of all beings, situated within the circle.
It shall serve as the cause for joining together a thousand vajra-weapons;
meditating upon the Supreme Self, one should cast water upwards.
Beyond the dust of the world is that which is the word "Om," the sound, the resonance, the unstruck sound (anāhata), and the syllable Aham;
I am that, I am the light, the light of the sun, I am Śiva.
This semen is the light of the self; this, indeed, is the light of all. You are Hara (*); know my evil! You are my portion (*); know my evil! You are completely purified (*); know my evil!

O Yādava, you are the *praṇava* who speaks over the snow... may there be a stream for the wise one... bhuvaḥ bhuvaḥ bhuvaḥ. Having performed the twilight devotion (*saṃdhyā*)... by whom the blue splendor and dust...
O illustrious Sandhyā-devī, who is adorned, whose lotus-hands grant boons and fearlessness, who possesses three eyes and has the moon as her crest-jewel,
you who are saluted by all the gods!
By the mere act of worshipping you, one is liberated from all sins.
She who is the barren one, whose form is the universe, who is perfectly steady,
the Sovereign, the absolute Power, and the source of the three principles.
Oh, how great is the divine Sarasvatī at the twilight hour, possessing many forms!
O you who are ageless, immortal, eternal, and the source of Brahman, salutations be unto you!
Having recited the Praṇava, the Supreme Self, endowed with devotion—
One should meditate upon one's own self as that [reality] and prostrate on the ground like a staff,
from the world of Brahmā down to the entire Lokāloka mountain.
Homage again and again to those twice-born gods who dwell here. May those beings depart who roam about, and those beings who are stationed upon the earth;
may those beings who create obstacles go away by the command of Śiva.
These fierce spirits, piśācas, and others are indeed the burden of the earth.
One should commence the rite of Brahman without contradicting these [deities].
O Goddess Earth, you support the worlds; you, O Goddess, are supported by Viṣṇu.
Therefore, O Goddess, support me and make this seat pure.
I bow to Gāyatrī, who is endowed with faces possessing the lusters of pearl, coral, gold, sapphire, and white;
whose crown is bound with a digit of the moon; who consists of the nature of the syllables that express the meaning of reality;
and who holds the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, a goad, a whip, a bright skull, and a cord.
I worship her who carries in her hands a conch, a discus, and a pair of lotuses.
To Yama, to Dharmarāja, to Mṛtyu, and to Antaka;
to Vaivasvata, to Kāla, and to Sarvabhūtakṣaya—[to these I offer salutations].
Salutations indeed to Odumbara, Dadhnya, Nīla, Parameṣṭhin,
Vṛkodara, Citra, and Citragupta. O Acyuta,
whose abode is Dvārakā and who holds the conch, discus, and mace in your hands!
O Govinda, O lotus-eyed one, protect me who have come to you for refuge.
Salutation to Savitṛ, the sole eye of the world, the cause of the origin, maintenance, and destruction of the universe;
who consists of the three Vedas, who sustains the nature of the three *guṇas*, and whose essence is Viriñci, Nārāyaṇa, and Śaṅkara.
Just as water fallen from the sky flows toward the ocean, so [does everything lead to him].
He goes toward Śaṅkara, who is saluted by all the gods.
I shall now describe the meditation on Agni for the sake of accomplishing the purpose of all fire-offerings (*homa*):
he has two faces, one heart, four ears, two nostrils,
two mouths, six eyes, is tawny (*piṅgala*), and possesses seven hands.
It has three girdles, three feet, and is endowed with seven tongues of flame.
He has four horns, is mounted upon a bull, and possesses a radiance equal to the rising sun;
he is endowed with a sacred thread and adorned with a crown of matted locks.
In the left portion, he has four hands, and in the right portion, three hands;
in the right hands are the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles, a rosary, and a spear;
and in the left hands are a javelin, a fan, and a vessel of clarified butter.
One should meditate upon the god Hutāśana as being turned toward oneself;
O Hutāśana, [accept] that which is deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, and deficient in devotion.
"O Lord, may that which has been offered by me as an oblation be fulfilled for you;
indeed, it constitutes all penances without exception, consisting essentially of the practice of austerity."
For all of them without exception, the supreme [practice] is the recollection of Śiva;
[this is] the acceptance by Parameṣṭhin, who has arisen from the nose.

May all my sins be dispelled by the nectar vomited by the full moon shining upon the crest of the crystal *liṅga* of light, which vibrates within the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*) extending from the surface of the waters to the vault of heaven.

For the sake of attaining his desired goal, a Brahmin should constantly recite the Rudrādhyāya without ceasing, even if it is not extensive; he should meditate on the Lord with rapid steps and consecrate Śiva.
May this [offering] always be for the satisfaction of the *preta*s—those whose selves are afflicted by hunger and thirst—wherever they may dwell, according to their pleasure.
In Raurava, the abode of merit, for those who dwell upon the lotuses and clouds;

Whoever remembers even a mere morsel of food, his sight shall never fail.

And may this happiness of mine, arising from its transformation, as well as that which is in my body, belong to Viṣṇu— the Lord who is the sole primary essence of all the senses, the gods, and embodied beings— and to no other. One should drink water three times with the right hand and wipe the lips twice;
then, having touched the base of the thumb, one should indeed touch the mouth and the other limbs.
One should touch the two nostrils with the index fingers;
then, by joining the middle fingers and the thumbs, one should touch the two eyes.
One should not touch the ears with the union of the thumb and the ring finger;
then, one should touch both shoulders with the union of the little finger and the thumb.
In the same manner, one should touch the navel and the heart with the palm of the hand;
thereafter, the remaining procedure for sipping water (ācamana) involves using all [the fingers].

One should grasp the throat with the thumb and the ring finger, and the nose with the index and middle fingers; or, by contracting [the fingers], one should hold [the breath] twelve times through the void.

Maṇipūraka is red in appearance, having ten petals, beginning with the letter *ḍa* and ending with the letter *pha*.

The city of Ājñā is red in hue, joined with the pair of seed-syllables of Lakṣmī and Vyākhyā;
above that is a thousand-petaled lotus facing downward, which is ever-expanded,
consisting of eternal bliss, and wherein I am Sadāśiva and Śakti is Maheśvarī.
One should meditate upon the Lord of the Gaṇas, the god who is the presiding lord of the hosts, who wears a serpent as a sacred thread, and who holds a noose and a goad.
One should constantly contemplate Brahmā as the Sun, bearing a rosary and a water-pot,
whose form is that of Brahman in the shape of the syllable 'A'.
One should meditate upon the god who holds the conch and the discus, the imperishable one who is beyond the syllable *u*,

One should meditate upon the form of Rudra in the form of the syllable *makāra*, holding a trident and a hand-drum in his hands, and bearing a rosary and a skull-bowl.
One should contemplate the form of the individual soul (*jīva*) situated in the middle of the *suṣumnā*, resembling pure crystal and possessing a radiance equal to the light of the moon.
One should meditate upon the Guru in the form of the Sun, the witness of the world, who dwells within the circle of the sky, for one blinded by the darkness of ignorance.
One should meditate upon the Supreme Self, who is truth, knowledge, and absolute reality, whose nature is pure consciousness, and who resembles ten million suns.

One should meditate upon the Goddess who stands by his side, possessing the luster of saffron, adorned with infinite ornaments, and having three eyes; she holds a book, a rosary, a deer-cub, and a lotus in her hands, and has the brilliance of refined gold.
Behind her, one should visualize [the deity] whose faces, arms, feet, flanks, belly, and chest are differentiated by the various colors [of the syllables].

I bow to that Bhāratī, who has a radiant braided hair adorned with a digit of the moon, who is as white as the moon or jasmine, whose excellent hands bear a rosary, a jar, and a book, who is slender, seated upon a lotus, resembling my own shadow, and burdened by the weight of her breasts and hips.
